# Python

Send email from Python, Django, Flask and FastAPI with the official delivrie package, verify webhooks, or use Django's SMTP backend.

The official [`delivrie`](https://pypi.org/project/delivrie/) package covers the whole API. It has no dependencies, works on Python 3.10 and later, and comes in sync and async versions. (Already using the `resend` package? Set `RESEND_API_URL=https://delivrie.io/api` and it talks to Delivrie; see [Migrate from Resend](/docs/migrate-from-resend).)

```bash
pip install delivrie
```

## Send an email

Create an API key in [API keys](https://delivrie.io/api-keys) and set it as `DELIVRIE_API_KEY`.

```python send.py
from delivrie import Delivrie

client = Delivrie()  # reads DELIVRIE_API_KEY

email = client.emails.send(
    from_="Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
    to="ada@example.com",
    subject="Welcome to Acme",
    html="<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>",
    idempotency_key="welcome-42",
)
print(email["id"])
```

`from` is a Python keyword, so pass `from_`, or pass a dict exactly like the REST API: `client.emails.send({"from": ..., "to": ..., ...})`. A `datetime` works for `scheduled_at`, `bytes` for attachment content and a dict for `tags`.

With an `idempotency_key`, the SDK retries network errors, rate limits and server errors safely: a retry returns the original email instead of sending a second one. Without one, sends aren't retried. See [Idempotency and retries](/docs/idempotency).

## Errors

Methods return the API's JSON as a dict and raise `DelivrieError` on failure:

```python
from delivrie import DelivrieError

try:
    client.emails.send(from_="Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>", to="ada@example.com", subject="Hi", text="Hello")
except DelivrieError as e:
    print(e.status_code, e.name, e.message)
```

Branch on `e.name` (see [Errors](/docs/errors)). `status_code` is 0 for `network_error` and `timeout`.

## Templates and attachments

```python
client.emails.send(
    from_="Acme <billing@mail.acme.com>",
    to="ada@example.com",
    template={"id": "invoice", "variables": {"first_name": "Ada", "total": "$20.00"}},
    attachments=[{"filename": "invoice.pdf", "content": open("invoice.pdf", "rb").read()}],
)
```

## Async (FastAPI)

```python main.py
from delivrie import AsyncDelivrie, DelivrieError
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()
client = AsyncDelivrie()

@app.post("/signup")
async def signup(email: str):
    try:
        sent = await client.emails.send(
            from_="Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
            to=email,
            subject="Welcome",
            html="<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>",
            idempotency_key=f"welcome-{email}",
        )
    except DelivrieError as e:
        raise HTTPException(502, e.message)
    return {"email_id": sent["id"]}
```

## Django

The simplest setup is Django's SMTP backend with the [SMTP relay](/docs/smtp), so `send_mail` and password-reset emails go through Delivrie:

```python settings.py
EMAIL_BACKEND = "django.core.mail.backends.smtp.EmailBackend"
EMAIL_HOST = "smtp.delivrie.io"
EMAIL_PORT = 587
EMAIL_USE_TLS = True
EMAIL_HOST_USER = "delivrie"
EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD = os.environ["DELIVRIE_API_KEY"]
DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL = "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>"
```

For templates, scheduling or tags, call the SDK from your views or tasks instead.

## Flask

```python app.py
from delivrie import Delivrie, DelivrieError
from flask import Flask, request

app = Flask(__name__)
client = Delivrie()

@app.post("/contact")
def contact():
    try:
        client.emails.send(
            from_="Website <forms@mail.acme.com>",
            to="team@acme.com",
            reply_to=request.form["email"],
            subject="New contact form message",
            text=request.form["message"],
        )
    except DelivrieError as e:
        return e.message, 502
    return "Sent", 200
```

## Verify webhooks

Pass the raw body, before parsing it:

```python webhooks.py
import os
from delivrie import verify_webhook, WebhookVerificationError

@app.post("/webhooks/delivrie")
def delivrie_webhook():
    try:
        event = verify_webhook(request.get_data(), request.headers, os.environ["DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"])
    except WebhookVerificationError:
        return "", 400
    if event["type"] == "email.bounced":
        ...
    return "", 204
```

In Django pass `request.body` and `request.headers`; in FastAPI, `await request.body()` and `request.headers`.

## Everything else

The client uses the same names as the [Node.js SDK](/docs/sdks), in snake_case: `client.domains`, `client.api_keys`, `client.webhooks`, `client.contacts`, `client.segments`, `client.broadcasts`, `client.templates`, `client.suppressions`, `client.events`, `client.automations`, `client.inbox` (threads, drafts, notes), `client.inboxes`, `client.ai`, `client.metrics`, `client.logs` and `client.usage`. For example, `client.broadcasts.duplicate(id)`, `client.contacts.import_contacts(csv=...)`, `client.emails.received_attachments(id)` and `client.templates.edit_content(id, ops=[...])`. For anything else, `client.request("GET", "/path")` calls the API directly.

## Without the SDK

The API is a single JSON request, so `requests` or `httpx` work too:

```python
import os, requests

res = requests.post(
    "https://delivrie.io/api/emails",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['DELIVRIE_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": "welcome-42"},
    json={"from": "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>", "to": "ada@example.com", "subject": "Welcome", "html": "<p>Hi</p>"},
    timeout=30,
)
res.raise_for_status()
print(res.json()["id"])
```


---

# PHP and Laravel

Send email from PHP and Laravel with Delivrie: the PHP SDK, Laravel's SMTP mailer, and webhook verification.

## Laravel

Laravel's mail system works with the [SMTP relay](/docs/smtp) out of the box, so `Mail::to(...)->send(...)`, notifications and password resets all go through Delivrie. Update `.env`:

```bash .env
MAIL_MAILER=smtp
MAIL_HOST=smtp.delivrie.io
MAIL_PORT=587
MAIL_ENCRYPTION=tls
MAIL_USERNAME=delivrie
MAIL_PASSWORD=dlv_your_key
MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=hello@mail.acme.com
MAIL_FROM_NAME="Acme"
```

Then clear the config cache (`php artisan config:clear`) and send as usual:

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Mail;
use App\Mail\OrderShipped;

Mail::to($user)->send(new OrderShipped($order));
```

Already on Laravel's `resend` mailer? Set `RESEND_BASE_URL=https://delivrie.io/api` and `RESEND_API_KEY=dlv_your_key` instead; see [Migrate from Resend](/docs/migrate-from-resend).

## The PHP SDK

PHP 8.1 or later, with only the curl and json extensions.

```bash
composer require delivrie/delivrie-php
```

```php send.php
<?php
require 'vendor/autoload.php';

$delivrie = new \Delivrie\Delivrie(getenv('DELIVRIE_API_KEY'));

$email = $delivrie->emails->send([
    'from' => 'Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>',
    'to' => 'ada@example.com',
    'subject' => 'Your receipt',
    'html' => '<p>Thanks for your order.</p>',
], ['idempotency_key' => 'order-1042']);

echo $email['id'];
```

Every method returns the API's JSON as an array. Errors throw `Delivrie\Exception\DelivrieException`, with `getStatusCode()`, `getErrorName()` (like `validation_error`) and `getMessage()`. With an idempotency key, the SDK retries rate limits, server errors and network errors for you, and a retry never sends twice.

Templates, attachments and scheduling:

```php
$delivrie->emails->send([
    'to' => 'ada@example.com',
    'template' => ['id' => 'welcome', 'variables' => ['name' => 'Ada']],
    'attachments' => [['path' => __DIR__ . '/invoice.pdf']],
    'scheduled_at' => 'tomorrow at 9am',
]);
```

With a template, `from` and `subject` are optional: the template's own are used. `path` reads the file and encodes it for you.

The SDK covers the whole API: `$delivrie->domains`, `apiKeys`, `webhooks`, `contacts`, `segments`, `broadcasts`, `templates`, `suppressions`, `events`, `automations`, `inbox` (threads, drafts, notes), `inboxes`, `ai`, `logs`, plus `usage()` and `metrics()`. For example, `$delivrie->broadcasts->duplicate($id)`, `$delivrie->contacts->import(['csv' => $csv])`, `$delivrie->emails->receivedAttachments($id)` and `$delivrie->templates->editContent($id, ['ops' => [...]])`.

In Laravel, bind it once in a service provider:

```php app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php
$this->app->singleton(\Delivrie\Delivrie::class, fn () => new \Delivrie\Delivrie(env('DELIVRIE_API_KEY')));
```

## WordPress

Use any SMTP plugin (WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP, Post SMTP) with host `smtp.delivrie.io`, port `587`, encryption TLS, username `delivrie` and an API key as the password. See [SMTP](/docs/smtp).

## Verify webhooks

```php webhook.php
<?php
$event = \Delivrie\Webhook::verify(
    file_get_contents('php://input'),   // the raw body, before decoding
    getallheaders(),
    getenv('DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),  // whsec_…
);
// $event['type'] is "email.delivered", "email.bounced", …
```

It throws `Delivrie\Exception\WebhookVerificationException` for a bad signature, or a request older than 5 minutes. In Laravel, pass `$request->getContent()` and `$request->headers->all()`, and exclude the route from CSRF protection.


---

# Ruby and Rails

Send email from Ruby and Rails with the official delivrie gem, or with Action Mailer over SMTP, and verify Delivrie webhooks.

The `delivrie` gem is the official Ruby SDK. It has no dependencies and works on Ruby 3.1 and later. Source: [github.com/bysurce/delivrie](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/sdk/ruby).

```bash
gem install delivrie
```

Or add `gem "delivrie"` to your Gemfile.

## Send an email

```ruby send.rb
require "delivrie"

delivrie = Delivrie::Client.new(ENV["DELIVRIE_API_KEY"])

email = delivrie.emails.send_email(
  from: "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
  to: "ada@example.com",
  subject: "Welcome",
  html: "<p>Welcome to Acme</p>",
)
puts email["id"]
```

Methods take keyword arguments or a Hash, with the API's field names (`reply_to`, `scheduled_at`), and return the API's JSON as a Hash with string keys. Without a key argument, the client reads `DELIVRIE_API_KEY`.

## Errors, retries and idempotency

A failed request raises `Delivrie::Error` with `status`, `name` (like `validation_error`, see [Errors](/docs/errors)) and `message`. Problems that never reach the API have `status` 0 and the name `network_error` or `timeout`.

```ruby
begin
  delivrie.emails.send_email({ from: "Acme <hi@acme.com>", to: user.email, template: { id: "welcome" } }, idempotency_key: "welcome-#{user.id}")
rescue Delivrie::Error => e
  Rails.logger.warn("Delivrie #{e.status} #{e.name}: #{e.message}")
end
```

`GET` and `DELETE` requests are retried twice on rate limits, `5xx` responses and network failures. Sends are retried only with `idempotency_key`, which makes a retry return the original email instead of sending another. Options: `Delivrie::Client.new(key, timeout: 30, max_retries: 2, base_url: "https://delivrie.io/api")`.

## Attachments

`path` can be a local file (the gem reads it and sends it as base64) or a public `https://` URL (Delivrie downloads it):

```ruby
delivrie.emails.send_email(
  from: "Billing <billing@mail.acme.com>", to: "ada@example.com", subject: "Your invoice", text: "Attached.",
  attachments: [{ path: "tmp/invoice-1042.pdf" }, { path: "https://acme.com/terms.pdf" }],
)
```

## Rails (Action Mailer)

Point Action Mailer at the [SMTP relay](/docs/smtp) and your existing mailers, Devise emails and `deliver_later` jobs send through Delivrie:

```ruby config/environments/production.rb
config.action_mailer.delivery_method = :smtp
config.action_mailer.smtp_settings = {
  address: "smtp.delivrie.io",
  port: 587,
  user_name: "delivrie",
  password: ENV.fetch("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"),
  authentication: :plain,
  enable_starttls_auto: true,
}
config.action_mailer.default_options = { from: "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>" }
```

## Methods

| Resource | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `emails` | `send_email`, `send_batch`, `get`, `list`, `list_received`, `update`, `cancel`, `forward`, `attachments`, `received_attachments`, `share` |
| `domains` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `verify`, `update`, `delete` |
| `api_keys` | `create`, `list`, `update`, `delete` |
| `webhooks` | `create`, `list`, `deliveries`, `test`, `replay` |
| `contacts` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `import_contacts`, `get_import`, `list_imports` |
| `segments` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `contacts`, `add_contacts`, `remove_contacts` |
| `broadcasts` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `send_broadcast`, `cancel`, `duplicate`, `recipients`, `links`, `delete`, `get_content`, `edit_content` |
| `templates` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `publish`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `get_content`, `edit_content` |
| `suppressions` | `list`, `add`, `delete` |
| `events` | `send_event`, `list` |
| `automations` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `runs`, `publish`, `pause`, `resume`, `duplicate` |
| `inboxes` | `list`, `create`, `get`, `update`, `delete`, `agent_runs` |
| `inbox` | `threads`, `thread`, `update_thread`, `reply`, `run_agent`, `notes`, `add_note`, `delete_note`, `drafts`, `create_draft`, `update_draft`, `send_draft`, `discard_draft`, `labels` |
| `ai` | `draft`, `rewrite`, `subjects` |
| `logs` | `list`, `get` |

For anything else, `delivrie.request(:get, "/emails", query: { limit: 10 })` calls the API with the same auth, retries and errors. Every endpoint is in the [API reference](/docs/api).

## Verify webhooks

```ruby app/controllers/delivrie_webhooks_controller.rb
class DelivrieWebhooksController < ActionController::API
  def create
    event = Delivrie::Webhook.verify(request.raw_post, request.headers.to_h, ENV.fetch("DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"))
    # event["type"], event["data"]
    head :ok
  rescue Delivrie::WebhookVerificationError
    head :bad_request
  end
end
```

It checks the signature against the raw body, rejects requests older than five minutes, and accepts Rack-style header names (`HTTP_WEBHOOK_ID`). More in [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks).


---

# Go

Send email from Go with the Delivrie Go SDK: typed requests, idempotent retries, errors you can inspect, and webhook verification.

The Go SDK is standard library only and needs Go 1.21 or later.

```bash
go get github.com/bysurce/delivrie/sdk/go
```

The module moved from `github.com/codeddesigner/delivrie/sdk/go` in v0.2.0. Code that imports the old path keeps working on v0.1.0; to upgrade, change the import path and run `go get` again.

## Send an email

```go main.go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"

	delivrie "github.com/bysurce/delivrie/sdk/go"
)

func main() {
	client := delivrie.New(os.Getenv("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"))

	sent, err := client.Emails.Send(context.Background(), &delivrie.SendEmailRequest{
		From:    "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
		To:      []string{"ada@example.com"},
		Subject: "Your receipt",
		HTML:    "<p>Thanks for your order.</p>",
	}, delivrie.WithIdempotencyKey("order-1042"))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println(sent.ID)
}
```

The idempotency key makes the send safe to retry: the same key returns the original email instead of sending it again. With a key, the SDK also retries rate limits, server errors and network errors for you (twice, with backoff).

## Templates, attachments and scheduling

```go
client.Emails.Send(ctx, &delivrie.SendEmailRequest{
	To:          []string{"ada@example.com"},
	Template:    &delivrie.TemplateRef{ID: "welcome", Variables: map[string]any{"name": "Ada"}},
	Attachments: []delivrie.Attachment{{Filename: "invoice.pdf", Content: pdfBytes}},
	ScheduledAt: "tomorrow at 9am",
})
```

With a template, `From` and `Subject` are optional: the template's own are used. `Content` is the raw file; the SDK encodes it. `ScheduledAt` takes an RFC 3339 time or a phrase like `in 1 hour` (UTC), up to 30 days ahead.

## Handle errors

API errors are `*delivrie.Error`, with the HTTP status, Delivrie's error name and a message:

```go
if err != nil {
	var apiErr *delivrie.Error
	if errors.As(err, &apiErr) && apiErr.Name == "validation_error" {
		log.Printf("fix the request: %s", apiErr.Message)
	}
}
```

`delivrie.IsNotFound(err)` and `delivrie.IsRateLimited(err)` cover the common checks. See [Errors](/docs/errors) for every name.

## Everything else

The client covers the whole API: `client.Domains`, `client.APIKeys`, `client.Webhooks`, `client.Contacts`, `client.Segments`, `client.Broadcasts`, `client.Templates`, `client.Suppressions`, `client.Events`, `client.Automations`, `client.Inbox` (threads, drafts, notes), `client.Inboxes`, `client.AI`, `client.Metrics`, `client.Logs` and `client.Usage`. For example, `client.Broadcasts.Duplicate`, `client.Contacts.Import`, `client.Emails.ReceivedAttachments` and `client.Templates.EditContent`.

```go
domain, _ := client.Domains.Create(ctx, &delivrie.CreateDomainRequest{Name: "mail.acme.com"})
for _, r := range domain.Records {
	fmt.Println(r.Type, r.Name, r.Value)
}
```

`client.Do(ctx, "GET", "/path", nil, &out)` calls any endpoint the SDK doesn't wrap yet.

## Verify webhooks

```go webhook.go
func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
	event, err := delivrie.VerifyWebhook(body, r.Header, os.Getenv("DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"))
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "invalid signature", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	log.Println(event.Type) // "email.delivered", "email.bounced", …
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}
```

Read the body before decoding it: the signature covers the exact bytes. Requests older than 5 minutes are rejected as replays. See [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks).

Already using `resend-go`? Set `RESEND_BASE_URL=https://delivrie.io/api/` and it talks to Delivrie; see [Migrate from Resend](/docs/migrate-from-resend).


---

# Rust

Send email from Rust with the official delivrie crate: async requests with reqwest and serde_json, typed errors, idempotent retries and webhook verification.

The `delivrie` crate is the official Rust SDK. It's async, built on `reqwest` with rustls, and takes anything that implements `serde::Serialize`. Source: [github.com/bysurce/delivrie](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/sdk/rust).

```bash
cargo add delivrie serde_json
cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread
```

## Send an email

```rust src/main.rs
use serde_json::json;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> delivrie::Result<()> {
    let delivrie = delivrie::Client::new(std::env::var("DELIVRIE_API_KEY").expect("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"));

    let email = delivrie
        .emails()
        .send(&json!({
            "from": "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
            "to": "ada@example.com",
            "subject": "Welcome",
            "html": "<p>Welcome to Acme</p>",
        }))
        .await?;
    println!("{}", email["id"]);
    Ok(())
}
```

Methods return the API's JSON as a `serde_json::Value`. Pass your own structs instead of `json!` when you prefer types: any `#[derive(Serialize)]` value works. `Client` is cheap to clone and safe to share between tasks.

## Errors, retries and idempotency

```rust
match delivrie.emails().send_idempotent(&email, &format!("welcome-{user_id}")).await {
    Ok(sent) => println!("sent {}", sent["id"]),
    Err(e) => eprintln!("{} {}: {e}", e.status(), e.name()),
}
```

`delivrie::Error` is `Api { status, name, message }`, `Network`, `Timeout` or `Invalid`; `status()` and `name()` work on all of them (see [Errors](/docs/errors)). `GET` and `DELETE` requests are retried twice on rate limits, `5xx` responses and network failures. Sends are retried only through the `_idempotent` methods, so a retry never sends twice.

```rust
let delivrie = delivrie::Client::builder()
    .api_key(key)
    .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))
    .max_retries(3)
    .build()?;
```

## Attachments

Send base64 `content`, or a public `https://` URL as `path` for Delivrie to download:

```rust
use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, Engine};

let pdf = std::fs::read("invoice-1042.pdf")?;
delivrie.emails().send(&json!({
    "from": "Billing <billing@mail.acme.com>",
    "to": "ada@example.com",
    "subject": "Your invoice",
    "text": "Attached.",
    "attachments": [{ "filename": "invoice-1042.pdf", "content": STANDARD.encode(pdf) }],
})).await?;
```

## Methods

| Resource | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `emails()` | `send`, `send_batch`, `get`, `list`, `list_received`, `update`, `cancel`, `forward`, `attachments`, `received_attachments`, `share` |
| `domains()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `verify`, `update`, `delete` |
| `api_keys()` | `create`, `list`, `update`, `delete` |
| `webhooks()` | `create`, `list`, `deliveries`, `test`, `replay` |
| `contacts()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `import_contacts`, `get_import`, `list_imports` |
| `segments()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `contacts`, `add_contacts`, `remove_contacts` |
| `broadcasts()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `send`, `cancel`, `duplicate`, `recipients`, `links`, `delete`, `get_content`, `edit_content` |
| `templates()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `publish`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `get_content`, `edit_content` |
| `suppressions()` | `list`, `add`, `delete` |
| `events()` | `send`, `list` |
| `automations()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `runs`, `publish`, `pause`, `resume`, `duplicate` |
| `inboxes()` | `list`, `create`, `get`, `update`, `delete`, `agent_runs` |
| `inbox()` | `threads`, `thread`, `update_thread`, `reply`, `run_agent`, `notes`, `add_note`, `delete_note`, `drafts`, `create_draft`, `update_draft`, `send_draft`, `discard_draft`, `labels` |
| `ai()` | `draft`, `rewrite`, `subjects` |
| `logs()` | `list`, `get` |

Methods with a body take `&impl Serialize`; list methods take query pairs like `&[("limit", "10")]`. For anything else, `delivrie.request("GET", "/emails", None::<&serde_json::Value>, &[("limit", "10")], None)` calls the API with the same auth, retries and errors. Every endpoint is in the [API reference](/docs/api).

## Verify webhooks

```rust
// axum
async fn webhook(headers: axum::http::HeaderMap, body: String) -> axum::http::StatusCode {
    let pairs = headers.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.to_str().unwrap_or("")));
    match delivrie::webhook::verify(&body, pairs, &std::env::var("DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET").unwrap()) {
        Ok(event) => {
            // event["type"], event["data"]
            axum::http::StatusCode::OK
        }
        Err(_) => axum::http::StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
    }
}
```

It checks the signature against the raw body and rejects requests older than five minutes. More in [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks).


---

# Java and Spring

Send email from Java, Spring Boot and Kotlin with the official Delivrie Java SDK: no dependencies, idempotent retries, errors you can inspect, and webhook verification.

The Delivrie Java SDK has no dependencies and runs on Java 17 and later, including Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut and Kotlin. Source: [github.com/bysurce/delivrie](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/sdk/java).

```xml pom.xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.delivrie</groupId>
  <artifactId>delivrie-java</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
</dependency>
```

```kotlin build.gradle.kts
implementation("io.delivrie:delivrie-java:0.1.0")
```

## Send an email

```java
import io.delivrie.Delivrie;
import java.util.Map;

Delivrie delivrie = new Delivrie(System.getenv("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"));

Map<String, Object> email = delivrie.emails().send(Map.of(
    "from", "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
    "to", "ada@example.com",
    "subject", "Welcome",
    "html", "<p>Welcome to Acme</p>"));
System.out.println(email.get("id"));
```

Methods take a `Map` with the API's field names and return the API's JSON as a `Map<String, Object>` (objects as maps, arrays as lists, numbers as `Long` or `Double`). The client is thread-safe: in Spring, declare it once as a `@Bean`.

## Errors, retries and idempotency

```java
try {
  delivrie.emails().send(Map.of("from", "Acme <hi@acme.com>", "to", user.email(),
      "template", Map.of("id", "welcome")), "welcome-" + user.id());
} catch (DelivrieException e) {
  log.warn("Delivrie {} {}: {}", e.status(), e.name(), e.getMessage());
}
```

`DelivrieException` has the HTTP `status()` (0 for network errors and timeouts), Delivrie's error `name()` (see [Errors](/docs/errors)) and the message. `GET` and `DELETE` requests are retried twice on rate limits, `5xx` responses and network failures. Sends are retried only when you pass an idempotency key (the second argument of `send`), so a retry never sends twice.

```java
Delivrie delivrie = Delivrie.builder()
    .apiKey(key)
    .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .maxRetries(3)
    .build();
```

## Attachments

```java
delivrie.emails().send(Map.of(
    "from", "Billing <billing@mail.acme.com>", "to", "ada@example.com", "subject", "Your invoice", "text", "Attached.",
    "attachments", List.of(Delivrie.attachment(Path.of("invoice-1042.pdf")), Map.of("path", "https://acme.com/terms.pdf"))));
```

`Delivrie.attachment(path)` reads a local file; a `path` with an `https://` URL is downloaded by Delivrie.

## Spring Boot over SMTP

If you'd rather keep `JavaMailSender`, point it at the [SMTP relay](/docs/smtp):

```properties application.properties
spring.mail.host=smtp.delivrie.io
spring.mail.port=587
spring.mail.username=delivrie
spring.mail.password=${DELIVRIE_API_KEY}
spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.auth=true
spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.starttls.enable=true
```

## Methods

| Resource | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `emails()` | `send`, `sendBatch`, `get`, `list`, `listReceived`, `update`, `cancel`, `forward`, `attachments`, `receivedAttachments`, `share` |
| `domains()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `verify`, `update`, `delete` |
| `apiKeys()` | `create`, `list`, `update`, `delete` |
| `webhooks()` | `create`, `list`, `deliveries`, `test`, `replay` |
| `contacts()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `importContacts`, `getImport`, `listImports` |
| `segments()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `contacts`, `addContacts`, `removeContacts` |
| `broadcasts()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `send`, `cancel`, `duplicate`, `recipients`, `links`, `delete`, `getContent`, `editContent` |
| `templates()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `publish`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `getContent`, `editContent` |
| `suppressions()` | `list`, `add`, `delete` |
| `events()` | `send`, `list` |
| `automations()` | `create`, `get`, `list`, `update`, `delete`, `runs`, `publish`, `pause`, `resume`, `duplicate` |
| `inboxes()` | `list`, `create`, `get`, `update`, `delete`, `agentRuns` |
| `inbox()` | `threads`, `thread`, `updateThread`, `reply`, `runAgent`, `notes`, `addNote`, `deleteNote`, `drafts`, `createDraft`, `updateDraft`, `sendDraft`, `discardDraft`, `labels` |
| `ai()` | `draft`, `rewrite`, `subjects` |
| `logs()` | `list`, `get` |

List methods also take a `Map` of query parameters, like `delivrie.emails().list(Map.of("limit", 10))`. For anything else, `delivrie.request("GET", "/emails", null, Map.of("limit", 10), null)` calls the API with the same auth, retries and errors. Every endpoint is in the [API reference](/docs/api).

## Verify webhooks

```java
@PostMapping("/webhooks/delivrie")
ResponseEntity<Void> webhook(@RequestBody String body, @RequestHeader Map<String, String> headers) {
  try {
    Map<String, Object> event = Webhook.verify(body, headers, System.getenv("DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"));
    // event.get("type"), event.get("data")
    return ResponseEntity.ok().build();
  } catch (WebhookVerificationException e) {
    return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build();
  }
}
```

It checks the signature against the raw body and rejects requests older than five minutes. More in [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks).


---

# Supabase

Use Delivrie with Supabase: send Supabase Auth emails (sign-up, magic links, password resets) through custom SMTP, and send app email from Edge Functions.

## Send Supabase Auth emails through Delivrie

Supabase's built-in email service is rate-limited and meant for testing. Point Auth at the [SMTP relay](/docs/smtp) so confirmation, magic-link and password-reset emails come from your own domain:

1. In the Supabase dashboard, open **Authentication → Emails → SMTP Settings** and turn on **Enable custom SMTP**.
2. Fill in:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Sender email | An address on your verified domain, like `auth@mail.acme.com` |
| Sender name | Your app's name |
| Host | `smtp.delivrie.io` |
| Port | `587` (or `465`) |
| Username | `delivrie` |
| Password | A Delivrie API key (a sending access key is enough) |

3. Save, then raise the email rate limit under **Authentication → Rate Limits** to suit your app.

Every Auth email then shows up in [Emails](https://delivrie.io/emails) with its delivery status.

## Send from an Edge Function

```ts supabase/functions/send-welcome/index.ts
import { Delivrie } from "npm:delivrie";

const delivrie = new Delivrie(Deno.env.get("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"));

Deno.serve(async (req) => {
  const { email, name } = await req.json();
  const { data, error } = await delivrie.emails.send({
    from: "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
    to: email,
    subject: `Welcome, ${name}`,
    html: `<p>Thanks for joining Acme.</p>`,
  }, { idempotencyKey: `welcome-${email}` });

  if (error) return Response.json({ error: error.message }, { status: 502 });
  return Response.json({ id: data.id });
});
```

Set the secret and deploy:

```bash
supabase secrets set DELIVRIE_API_KEY=dlv_your_key
supabase functions deploy send-welcome
```

## Send when a row changes

To email users when something happens in your database (a new order, say), create a Database Webhook in **Database → Webhooks** that calls your Edge Function on `INSERT`. The function receives `{ type, table, record }` and sends the email with `record` fields.

## Webhooks into Supabase

Receive Delivrie events in an Edge Function with `verifyWebhook` from `npm:delivrie`, then write bounces or opens to a table. Deploy it with `--no-verify-jwt`, because Delivrie authenticates with its signature rather than a Supabase JWT:

```bash
supabase functions deploy delivrie-webhooks --no-verify-jwt
```


---

# .NET and C#

Send email from C#, ASP.NET Core and any .NET 8 app with the official Delivrie NuGet package: async methods, idempotent retries, errors you can inspect, and webhook verification.

The `Delivrie` NuGet package is the official .NET SDK. It's async, needs nothing beyond the .NET 8 runtime, and works in ASP.NET Core, worker services, Azure Functions and console apps. Source: [github.com/bysurce/delivrie](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/sdk/dotnet).

```bash
dotnet add package Delivrie
```

## Send an email

```csharp
using Delivrie;

var delivrie = new DelivrieClient(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"));

var email = await delivrie.Emails.SendAsync(new
{
    from = "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
    to = "ada@example.com",
    subject = "Welcome",
    html = "<p>Welcome to Acme</p>",
});
Console.WriteLine(email["id"]);
```

Methods take any object that serialises to the API's JSON (anonymous objects, dictionaries, your own classes, or a `JsonNode`) and return the response as a `JsonObject`. In ASP.NET Core, register one client: `builder.Services.AddSingleton(new DelivrieClient(builder.Configuration["Delivrie:ApiKey"]));`.

## Errors, retries and idempotency

```csharp
try
{
    await delivrie.Emails.SendAsync(new { from = "Acme <hi@acme.com>", to = user.Email, template = new { id = "welcome" } }, idempotencyKey: $"welcome-{user.Id}");
}
catch (DelivrieException e)
{
    logger.LogWarning("Delivrie {Status} {Name}: {Message}", e.Status, e.Name, e.Message);
}
```

`DelivrieException` has the HTTP `Status` (0 for network errors and timeouts), Delivrie's error `Name` (see [Errors](/docs/errors)) and the message. `GET` and `DELETE` requests are retried twice on rate limits, `5xx` responses and network failures. Sends are retried only with an `idempotencyKey`, so a retry never sends twice. Every method takes a `CancellationToken`.

```csharp
var delivrie = new DelivrieClient(key, new DelivrieClientOptions { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10), MaxRetries = 3 });
```

## Attachments

```csharp
await delivrie.Emails.SendAsync(new
{
    from = "Billing <billing@mail.acme.com>", to = "ada@example.com", subject = "Your invoice", text = "Attached.",
    attachments = new object[] { DelivrieClient.Attachment("invoice-1042.pdf"), new { path = "https://acme.com/terms.pdf" } },
});
```

## Methods

| Resource | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `Emails` | `SendAsync`, `SendBatchAsync`, `GetAsync`, `ListAsync`, `ListReceivedAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `CancelAsync`, `ForwardAsync`, `AttachmentsAsync`, `ReceivedAttachmentsAsync`, `ShareAsync` |
| `Domains` | `CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `ListAsync`, `VerifyAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync` |
| `ApiKeys` | `CreateAsync`, `ListAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync` |
| `Webhooks` | `CreateAsync`, `ListAsync`, `DeliveriesAsync`, `TestAsync`, `ReplayAsync` |
| `Contacts` | `CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `ListAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `ImportContactsAsync`, `GetImportAsync`, `ListImportsAsync` |
| `Segments` | `CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `ListAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `ContactsAsync`, `AddContactsAsync`, `RemoveContactsAsync` |
| `Broadcasts` | `CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `ListAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `SendAsync`, `CancelAsync`, `DuplicateAsync`, `RecipientsAsync`, `LinksAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `GetContentAsync`, `EditContentAsync` |
| `Templates` | `CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `ListAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `PublishAsync`, `DuplicateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `GetContentAsync`, `EditContentAsync` |
| `Suppressions` | `ListAsync`, `AddAsync`, `DeleteAsync` |
| `Events` | `SendAsync`, `ListAsync` |
| `Automations` | `CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `ListAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `RunsAsync`, `PublishAsync`, `PauseAsync`, `ResumeAsync`, `DuplicateAsync` |
| `Inboxes` | `ListAsync`, `CreateAsync`, `GetAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `AgentRunsAsync` |
| `Inbox` | `ThreadsAsync`, `ThreadAsync`, `UpdateThreadAsync`, `ReplyAsync`, `RunAgentAsync`, `NotesAsync`, `AddNoteAsync`, `DeleteNoteAsync`, `DraftsAsync`, `CreateDraftAsync`, `UpdateDraftAsync`, `SendDraftAsync`, `DiscardDraftAsync`, `LabelsAsync` |
| `Ai` | `DraftAsync`, `RewriteAsync`, `SubjectsAsync` |
| `Logs` | `ListAsync`, `GetAsync` |

List methods take an optional `IDictionary<string, object?>` of query parameters. For anything else, `delivrie.RequestAsync("GET", "/emails", query: new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["limit"] = 10 })` calls the API with the same auth, retries and errors. Every endpoint is in the [API reference](/docs/api).

## Verify webhooks

```csharp
app.MapPost("/webhooks/delivrie", async (HttpRequest req) =>
{
    var body = await new StreamReader(req.Body).ReadToEndAsync();
    try
    {
        var evt = Webhook.Verify(body, name => req.Headers[name].FirstOrDefault(), builder.Configuration["DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]!);
        // evt["type"], evt["data"]
        return Results.Ok();
    }
    catch (WebhookVerificationException)
    {
        return Results.BadRequest();
    }
});
```

It checks the signature against the raw body and rejects requests older than five minutes. More in [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks).

# Cloudflare Workers

Send email from Cloudflare Workers, Pages Functions, Deno and Bun with the Delivrie SDK, which runs on web-standard APIs with no Node.js dependencies.

The `delivrie` SDK uses only `fetch` and Web Crypto, so it runs in Workers without the `nodejs_compat` flag.

```bash
npm install delivrie
npx wrangler secret put DELIVRIE_API_KEY
```

```ts src/index.ts
import { Delivrie, verifyWebhook } from "delivrie";

interface Env {
  DELIVRIE_API_KEY: string;
  DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: string;
}

export default {
  async fetch(req: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const url = new URL(req.url);
    const delivrie = new Delivrie(env.DELIVRIE_API_KEY); // Workers have no process.env: pass the key

    if (url.pathname === "/send" && req.method === "POST") {
      const { email } = await req.json<{ email: string }>();
      const { data, error } = await delivrie.emails.send({
        from: "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
        to: email,
        subject: "Hello from the edge",
        html: "<p>Sent from a Cloudflare Worker.</p>",
      });
      return error ? Response.json(error, { status: 502 }) : Response.json(data);
    }

    if (url.pathname === "/webhooks/delivrie" && req.method === "POST") {
      try {
        const event = await verifyWebhook({ payload: await req.text(), headers: req.headers, secret: env.DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET });
        console.log(event.type);
        return new Response("ok");
      } catch {
        return new Response("invalid signature", { status: 400 });
      }
    }

    return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });
  },
};
```

## Deno and Bun

```ts Deno
import { Delivrie } from "npm:delivrie";
const delivrie = new Delivrie(Deno.env.get("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"));
```

```ts Bun
import { Delivrie } from "delivrie"; // bun add delivrie
const delivrie = new Delivrie(); // reads DELIVRIE_API_KEY from the environment
```

## Vercel Edge and Netlify Edge

Vercel's Edge runtime exposes `process.env`, so `new Delivrie()` picks up `DELIVRIE_API_KEY` from your project settings. On Netlify Edge Functions, pass the key yourself: `new Delivrie(Netlify.env.get("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"))`.

# Claude Code, Cursor and Codex

Install the Delivrie plugin in Claude Code, Cursor or Codex to add email to your app with the right SDK, and to send test emails, check domains and logs, and edit templates from your coding agent.

The Delivrie plugin gives your coding agent two things:

- **Skills** that teach it to add email the safe way: the right SDK for your language, the key in `DELIVRIE_API_KEY`, a verified sender, idempotency keys, test addresses and signed webhooks. Plus skills for webhooks, editing email content and migrating from Resend.
- **Delivrie's [MCP server](/docs/mcp)**, so it can work with your account: send a test email and confirm delivery, list domains and their DNS status, read logs, create webhooks, and edit templates and broadcasts live in the Delivrie editor.

## Claude Code

```text
/plugin marketplace add bysurce/delivrie
/plugin install delivrie@delivrie
```

Then try `/delivrie-setup`, or ask "add a welcome email to this app with Delivrie".

## Cursor

Open **Settings → Plugins**, add the marketplace `bysurce/delivrie` and install **delivrie**. It also adds a `delivrie` rule that applies to your mail and webhook code.

## Codex

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add bysurce/delivrie
```

Then enable **Delivrie** in `/plugins`. In ChatGPT, use the [Delivrie app](/docs/mcp) instead.

## Signing in

The first time the agent calls a Delivrie tool, your browser opens Delivrie's sign-in. Choose the team and what the agent may do: **send**, **read** and **manage**. Leave out **manage** if it should only send test emails and read logs. Revoke access any time in [Settings → Connected apps](https://delivrie.io/settings/connected-apps).

The plugin's source is in [integrations/agent-plugin](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/integrations/agent-plugin).

# Zapier

Connect Delivrie to 7,000+ apps with Zapier: send emails and templates, sync contacts and segments, start automations, and trigger Zaps from deliveries, bounces, received mail, the Inbox and broadcasts.

## Connect

Add the **Delivrie** app in Zapier and paste an API key from [API keys](https://delivrie.io/api-keys). A full access key works with everything; a sending key is enough for **Send Email**.

## Triggers

Triggers are instant: when a Zap turns on, Delivrie creates a [webhook](/docs/webhooks) for it, and deletes it when the Zap turns off.

| Trigger | When it fires |
| --- | --- |
| Email Event | An email is delivered, bounces, is opened or clicked, is marked as spam, fails or is delayed (choose which) |
| New Received Email | Mail arrives at one of your [receiving](/docs/receiving) addresses |
| Contact Created or Updated | A contact is added, changes, unsubscribes or is deleted |
| New Inbox Message | A customer writes to one of your [inboxes](/docs/inbox) |
| Broadcast Sent | A broadcast finishes sending, with its stats |

## Actions

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Send Email | Sends an email you write in the Zap, or a published [template](/docs/templates) with variables. Optional attachment URL, schedule and idempotency key |
| Create or Update Contact | Adds a contact or updates the one with that email, with properties, and optionally adds it to a segment |
| Add Contacts to Segment | Adds contacts to a segment, creating any that don't exist |
| Send Event | Records an [event](/docs/automations) that starts automations |
| Unsubscribe Contact | Unsubscribes a contact from broadcasts |
| Find Contact (search) | Looks a contact up by email |

## Ideas

- **New Stripe customer → Create or Update Contact** with their plan as a property, then **Send Event** `customer.created` to start an onboarding automation.
- **Email Event (bounced) → Update row in Google Sheets or HubSpot** to flag the address.
- **New Typeform entry → Send Email** using a published `form-receipt` template.
- **New Inbox Message → Slack** so the team sees new conversations.

The app's source is in [integrations/zapier](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/integrations/zapier).


---

# n8n

Use Delivrie in n8n workflows with the n8n-nodes-delivrie community package: send emails and templates, manage contacts and segments, start automations, reply in the Inbox, and trigger workflows on Delivrie events.

## Install

In n8n, open **Settings → Community nodes → Install**, enter `n8n-nodes-delivrie` and confirm. Then create **Delivrie API** credentials with a key from [API keys](https://delivrie.io/api-keys).

On a self-hosted n8n you can also install it with `npm install n8n-nodes-delivrie` in your n8n custom folder.

## Delivrie node

| Resource | Operations |
| --- | --- |
| Email | Send, Send Template, Get, Get Many |
| Contact | Create or Update, Get, Unsubscribe, Delete |
| Segment | Add Contacts, Remove Contacts, Get Many |
| Event | Send (starts [automations](/docs/automations)) |
| Broadcast | Send or schedule, Get |
| Inbox | Get Threads (with [search](/docs/inbox)), Reply, Create Draft |

Send Email takes an optional attachment URL and idempotency key. For anything else, use n8n's **HTTP Request** node with the same **Delivrie API** credentials and any endpoint from the [API reference](/docs/api).

## Delivrie Trigger

Choose the events to listen for (deliveries, bounces, opens, clicks, received mail, contacts, broadcasts, Inbox messages and agent runs). Activating the workflow creates a Delivrie [webhook](/docs/webhooks) for it; deactivating it deletes the webhook. Every request's signature is checked with the webhook's secret, and requests that don't match are rejected.

## Ideas

- **Inbox message → AI agent → Create Draft**, so a person reviews each reply before it goes out.
- **Email bounced → Postgres**: mark the address as invalid in your own database.
- **Schedule → Get Many contacts from your CRM → Create or Update Contact** to keep segments in sync.

The package's source is in [integrations/n8n](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/integrations/n8n).

# Make

Use Delivrie in Make scenarios: send emails and templates, create contacts, add them to segments, start automations, call any API endpoint, and watch Delivrie events instantly.

## Connect

Add a **Delivrie** module to a scenario and create a connection with an API key from [API keys](https://delivrie.io/api-keys).

## Modules

| Module | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Watch Events | Instant trigger | Runs the scenario on the Delivrie events you choose: deliveries, bounces, spam complaints, opens, clicks, received mail, contacts, broadcasts and Inbox messages |
| Send an Email | Action | Sends an email or a published [template](/docs/templates), with attachments by URL and an idempotency key |
| Create or Update a Contact | Action | Adds a contact or updates the one with that email, with properties and a segment |
| Add Contacts to a Segment | Action | Adds contacts, creating any that don't exist |
| Send an Event | Action | Records an [event](/docs/automations) that starts automations |
| Make an API Call | Universal | Calls any endpoint in the [API reference](/docs/api) with your connection |

Watch Events creates a Delivrie [webhook](/docs/webhooks) for the scenario and deletes it when you remove the trigger.

## Without the app

Every Delivrie endpoint also works from Make's **HTTP → Make a request** module: `https://delivrie.io/api/emails`, method `POST`, header `Authorization: Bearer <your API key>`, body type JSON.

The app's source is in [integrations/make](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/integrations/make).

# Auth0

Send Auth0's verification, password reset, welcome, MFA and invitation emails through Delivrie, with a custom email provider Action or over SMTP.

Auth0 sends sign-up verification, password resets, welcome messages, MFA codes and organization invitations. Send them through Delivrie so they come from your own domain and show up in your [logs](https://delivrie.io/logs).

## Option 1: Custom email provider (recommended)

1. In Auth0, open **Branding → Email Provider**, turn on **Use my own email provider** and choose **Custom Provider**.
2. Replace the Action code with this:

```js Custom Email Provider Action
exports.onExecuteCustomEmailProvider = async (event, api) => {
  const n = event.notification;
  const res = await fetch("https://delivrie.io/api/emails", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${event.secrets.DELIVRIE_API_KEY}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "Idempotency-Key": `auth0-${n.message_type}-${n.to}-${event.request?.id || ""}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      from: event.secrets.DELIVRIE_FROM || n.from,
      to: n.to,
      subject: n.subject,
      html: n.html,
      text: n.text,
      tags: [{ name: "source", value: "auth0" }],
    }),
  });
  if (res.ok) return;
  const body = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
  const reason = `Delivrie ${res.status}: ${body.message || ""}`;
  if (res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500) api.notification.retry(reason);
  else api.notification.drop(reason);
};
```

3. Add two secrets to the Action: `DELIVRIE_API_KEY` (a [sending key](https://delivrie.io/api-keys) is enough) and `DELIVRIE_FROM`, a sender on your verified domain like `Acme <auth@mail.acme.com>`.
4. Deploy, then use **Send test email**.

Rate limits and server errors are retried by Auth0; an invalid address is dropped and logged. The full version, with tests, is in [integrations/auth0](https://github.com/bysurce/delivrie/tree/main/integrations/auth0).

## Option 2: SMTP

Choose **SMTP Provider** instead and enter:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| From | An address on your verified domain |
| Host | `smtp.delivrie.io` |
| Port | `587` |
| Username | `delivrie` |
| Password | Your Delivrie API key |

See [SMTP relay](/docs/smtp) for details.


---

# Vercel

Add Delivrie to your Vercel projects: the integration creates an API key and sets DELIVRIE_API_KEY on the projects you choose, for production, preview and development.

## Connect from Vercel

1. Add the **Delivrie** integration from Vercel's integrations page and choose the Vercel team.
2. Vercel brings you to Delivrie. Sign in, pick the Delivrie team, then choose the Vercel projects that send email.
3. Choose **Sending only** (recommended) or **Full access**, and select **Connect**.

Delivrie creates an API key and adds it to each project as `DELIVRIE_API_KEY`, encrypted, for production, preview and development. Redeploy, and your code can read it:

```ts app/api/welcome/route.ts
import { Delivrie } from "delivrie";

const delivrie = new Delivrie(); // reads DELIVRIE_API_KEY

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { email } = await req.json();
  const { data, error } = await delivrie.emails.send({
    from: "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
    to: email,
    subject: "Welcome to Acme",
    html: "<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>",
  }, { idempotencyKey: `welcome-${email}` });
  return Response.json(error ?? data, { status: error ? 400 : 200 });
}
```

## Disconnect

Remove the integration in Vercel, or in Delivrie under [Settings → Integrations](https://delivrie.io/settings/integrations). Delivrie deletes the API key and removes `DELIVRIE_API_KEY` from the projects.

## Without the integration

Create a key in [API keys](https://delivrie.io/api-keys) and add it yourself: `vercel env add DELIVRIE_API_KEY`. See [Next.js](/docs/nextjs) for complete examples.


---

# Send an email

Everything about POST /emails: every field, display names, multiple recipients, cc and bcc, reply-to, HTML and text, attachments and inline images, tags, custom headers, scheduling and batch sending.

`POST https://delivrie.io/api/emails` sends one email. It returns as soon as the email is accepted, with its id; delivery happens in the background.

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/emails \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order-1042-receipt" \
  -d '{
    "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
    "to": ["ada@example.com"],
    "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
    "html": "<p>Order <b>#1042</b> is on its way.</p>",
    "tags": [{ "name": "category", "value": "receipt" }]
  }'
```

```ts Node.js
const { data, error } = await delivrie.emails.send({
  from: "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
  to: ["ada@example.com"],
  subject: "Your order is confirmed",
  html: "<p>Order <b>#1042</b> is on its way.</p>",
  tags: [{ name: "category", value: "receipt" }],
}, { idempotencyKey: "order-1042-receipt" });
```

```python Python
res = requests.post(
    "https://delivrie.io/api/emails",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Idempotency-Key": "order-1042-receipt"},
    json={
        "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
        "to": ["ada@example.com"],
        "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
        "html": "<p>Order <b>#1042</b> is on its way.</p>",
        "tags": [{"name": "category", "value": "receipt"}],
    },
)
```

Response:

```json
{ "id": "4ef9a417-02e9-4d39-ad75-9611e0fcc33c" }
```

## Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | Yes | `"Name <address@domain>"` or `"address@domain"`. The domain must be verified in your team. |
| `to` | string or string[] | Yes | Up to 50 addresses. |
| `subject` | string | Yes, unless you use `template` | |
| `html` | string | One of `html`, `text` or `template` | |
| `text` | string | | Plain-text version. Generated from `html` when you leave it out. |
| `cc`, `bcc` | string or string[] | | |
| `reply_to` | string or string[] | | Where replies go. |
| `template` | object | | `{ "id": "alias-or-id", "variables": { ... } }`. See [Templates](/docs/templates). |
| `scheduled_at` | string | | When to send. See [Scheduling](#scheduling). |
| `tags` | object[] | | `[{ "name": "...", "value": "..." }]`. Returned in webhook events. |
| `headers` | object | | Custom headers, like `{ "X-Order-Id": "1042" }`. |
| `attachments` | object[] | | See [Attachments](#attachments). |

Send the `Idempotency-Key` header too, so a retried request never sends twice. See [Idempotency and retries](/docs/idempotency).

## Senders and display names

`from` must use a domain you've verified in [Domains](https://delivrie.io/domains), including any subdomain of it. Add a display name in angle-bracket form: `"Acme Support <support@mail.acme.com>"`. If the name has commas or other punctuation, wrap it in quotes: `"\"Acme, Inc.\" <hello@mail.acme.com>"`.

Until your domain is verified, send from `onboarding@delivrie.io` to the [test addresses](/docs/test-mode) and to members of your team.

## Recipients

Each email can have up to 50 addresses in `to`. Everyone in `to` and `cc` sees each other; use `bcc` to hide recipients. To send different content to each person (a receipt per customer, say), send one email each, or up to 100 at a time with [batch sending](#batch-sending).

Addresses on your [suppression list](/docs/suppressions) are skipped automatically. If every recipient is suppressed, the email's status becomes `suppressed` and nothing is sent.

## HTML and plain text

Send `html`, `text`, or both. When you only send `html`, Delivrie builds the plain-text part for you, which helps deliverability. Inline your CSS (most email clients ignore `<style>` blocks), keep the width under about 600px, and use absolute `https://` URLs for images and links.

## Attachments

Attach files as base64 `content`. The total size can be up to 40 MB per email.

```json
"attachments": [
  {
    "filename": "invoice-1042.pdf",
    "content": "JVBERi0xLjcKJc...",
    "content_type": "application/pdf"
  }
]
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `filename` | Required. Shown to the recipient. |
| `content` | Base64-encoded file. (The Node.js SDK also accepts a `Buffer` or `Uint8Array`.) Provide `content` or `path`. |
| `path` | A public `https://` URL to download the file from when the email is accepted. `filename` defaults to the URL's file name. |
| `content_type` | Optional. Worked out from the filename when you leave it out. |
| `content_id` | Optional. Set it to show the file inline (see below). |

Up to 20 attachments and 40 MB per email. Sent files are kept for 30 days, like the email's content: `GET /emails/:id/attachments` returns them with download links that work for an hour.

### Inline images

Give the attachment a `content_id` and reference it in your HTML with `cid:`:

```json
{
  "html": "<p>Your QR code:</p><img src=\"cid:qr-1042\" width=\"200\">",
  "attachments": [{ "filename": "qr.png", "content": "iVBORw0KGgo...", "content_id": "qr-1042" }]
}
```

## Tags

Tags label emails so you can find them later and route webhook events. Names and values can use ASCII letters, numbers, `_` and `-`, up to 256 characters each.

```json
"tags": [{ "name": "category", "value": "password_reset" }, { "name": "user_id", "value": "u_8812" }]
```

Tags come back in every webhook event as an object: `"tags": { "category": "password_reset", "user_id": "u_8812" }`.

## Custom headers

```json
"headers": { "X-Order-Id": "1042", "List-Unsubscribe": "<https://acme.com/unsubscribe?u=8812>" }
```

Delivrie builds `From`, `To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`, `Subject`, `Date`, `MIME-Version` and the content headers from your fields, and ignores those names in `headers`. Header values can't contain line breaks.

## Scheduling

Set `scheduled_at` to send later, up to 30 days ahead. It accepts:

- an ISO 8601 date: `"2026-12-01T09:00:00Z"` or `"2026-12-01T10:00:00+01:00"`
- a phrase, read as UTC: `"in 10 minutes"`, `"in 2 hours"`, `"tomorrow at 9am"`

The email gets status `scheduled`. Change the time with `PATCH /emails/:id` and `{ "scheduled_at": "..." }`, or cancel it with `POST /emails/:id/cancel`, any time before it sends. Times less than 30 seconds away send right away.

## Batch sending

`POST /emails/batch` takes an array of up to 100 emails, each with its own recipients and content, and returns their ids in the same order:

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/emails/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: digest-2026-11-14" \
  -d '[
    { "from": "Acme <hi@mail.acme.com>", "to": "ada@example.com", "subject": "Your digest", "html": "<p>Hi Ada</p>" },
    { "from": "Acme <hi@mail.acme.com>", "to": "sam@example.com", "subject": "Your digest", "html": "<p>Hi Sam</p>" }
  ]'
```

```json
{ "data": [{ "id": "4ef9a417-..." }, { "id": "9a1c22b0-..." }] }
```

Batch emails can't have attachments or `scheduled_at`. If any email in the batch is invalid, the whole batch is rejected and nothing is sent, so you can fix it and retry. To send the same email to a list of subscribers, use [broadcasts](/docs/broadcasts) instead.

## After you send

- Check status in [Emails](https://delivrie.io/emails), or with `GET /emails/:id`, which returns the email and its events. See [Statuses and events](/docs/email-status).
- Get pushed updates with [webhooks](/docs/webhooks).
- Share an email with someone outside your team with `POST /emails/:id/share` (optionally `{ "expires_in_hours": 72 }`, up to 720). The link shows the email and its delivery timeline without signing in. `DELETE /emails/:id/share` revokes it.
- If a send fails, the response says why. See [Errors](/docs/errors).


---

# Idempotency and retries

Make email sends safe to retry with the Idempotency-Key header, choose good keys, and know which errors to retry.

Networks fail. If your request times out, you can't tell whether the email went out. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header, and retrying with the same key returns the original email instead of sending a second one.

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/emails \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order-1042-receipt" \
  -d '{ "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>", "to": "ada@example.com", "subject": "Receipt", "html": "<p>Thanks!</p>" }'
```

The first request sends the email and returns `{ "id": "..." }`. Every later request with the same key, from the same team, returns the same `id` and sends nothing, even if the body changed.

## Choosing keys

Build the key from the business event the email belongs to, not from a random value made at send time:

| Email | Good key |
| --- | --- |
| Order receipt | `order-1042-receipt` |
| Welcome email | `welcome-user-8812` |
| Password reset | `reset-8812-2026-11-14T10:05` (one per reset request) |
| Weekly digest | `digest-user-8812-2026-w46` |

Keep keys under 256 characters. They're kept with the email, so the same key never sends twice for your team, however much later you retry. Use a new key when you really do want to send again.

Batch sends take one key for the whole batch (`POST /emails/batch` with `Idempotency-Key: digest-2026-11-14`). Retrying the batch returns the same ids in the same order.

## When to retry

| Response | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `2xx` | Done. |
| Network error or timeout | Retry with the same key, with backoff (1s, 2s, 4s...). |
| `5xx` | Retry with the same key, with backoff. |
| `429` with `daily_quota_exceeded`, `monthly_quota_exceeded` or `spending_cap_reached` | Don't retry. It won't succeed until the limit resets or your plan changes. Alert someone. |
| `4xx` (anything else) | Don't retry. Fix the request; the `message` says what's wrong. |

The [Node.js SDK](/docs/sdks) does this for you: pass `idempotencyKey` and it retries network errors and `5xx` responses up to twice. Without a key, it never retries a send.

## Queues and background jobs

If you send from a job queue (BullMQ, Sidekiq, Celery, Laravel queues, Inngest, Trigger.dev), derive the key from the job's identity, not the attempt. The queue can then retry the job freely and the customer still gets one email.

```ts
worker.process("send-receipt", async (job) => {
  const { error } = await delivrie.emails.send(receiptFor(job.data.orderId), {
    idempotencyKey: `order-${job.data.orderId}-receipt`,
  });
  if (error && error.statusCode >= 500) throw new Error(error.message); // let the queue retry
});
```

## SMTP

Messages sent through the [SMTP relay](/docs/smtp) are deduplicated by their `Message-ID` header, so an app that retries an SMTP send doesn't send twice.


---

# Templates

Create reusable email templates with variables and fallbacks, publish versions, and send them from the API by id or alias.

Templates keep email design out of your code. Build them in the dashboard's visual or HTML editor (or with the API), publish a version, and send by alias with just the data that changes.

## Create and publish

1. Open [Templates](https://delivrie.io/templates) and click **Create template**. Start from blank or from one of the ready-made templates (below).
2. Give it an **alias**, a stable name your code sends by, like `order-confirmation`.
3. Write the subject and body using variables (below), set a default From address, and click **Publish**.

Or with the API:

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/templates \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Order confirmation",
    "alias": "order-confirmation",
    "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
    "subject": "Order {{order_id}} confirmed",
    "html": "<p>Hi {{first_name|there}},</p><p>Order {{order_id}} is on its way.</p>"
  }'

curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/templates/order-confirmation/publish \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"
```

Only published versions can be sent. Editing a template doesn't change what's sent until you publish again, and every publish is kept in the version history so you can roll back.

## Ready-made templates

Delivrie includes 22 designed templates you can start from, each with its variables already set up:

| Category | Templates |
| --- | --- |
| Account | Welcome, Verify email, Sign-in link, Team invitation, Account closed |
| Security | Verification code, Password reset, Password changed, New sign-in alert |
| Billing | Payment receipt, Invoice, Payment failed, Trial ending, Subscription renewed |
| Commerce | Order confirmation, Order shipped, Cart reminder |
| Marketing | Newsletter, Product announcement, Feedback request, Event invitation, We miss you |

They use a card layout: your logo above a white card, the content inside it, and the footer below. They're built with email-safe table layouts and adapt to phone screens. Everything is editable after you create one. Transactional templates have no unsubscribe link; marketing ones do.

## Brand kit

On the Starter plan and above, set your brand once in [Settings → Brand](https://delivrie.io/settings/brand): logo, button and text colours, background, font, button corners, postal address, support email and social links. New templates are created with your brand already applied. To restyle a template or broadcast you already have, open it, click **Styles**, then **Apply brand kit**.

Use a PNG or JPG logo, at least twice the height it's shown at so it stays sharp on high-resolution screens. Most email apps don't show SVG images.

## Send a template

Pass `template` instead of `html`/`text`. `subject` and `from` are optional; the template's defaults are used when you leave them out.

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/emails \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "to": "ada@example.com",
    "template": {
      "id": "order-confirmation",
      "variables": { "first_name": "Ada", "order_id": "#1042" }
    }
  }'
```

```ts Node.js
await delivrie.emails.send({
  from: "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
  to: "ada@example.com",
  template: { id: "order-confirmation", variables: { first_name: "Ada", order_id: "#1042" } },
}); // `subject` comes from the template
```

```python Python
requests.post("https://delivrie.io/api/emails", headers=auth, json={
    "to": "ada@example.com",
    "template": {"id": "order-confirmation", "variables": {"first_name": "Ada", "order_id": "#1042"}},
})
```

`template.id` takes the template's id or its alias.

## Variables

| Syntax | Inserts | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{first_name}}` | The value, HTML-escaped | Anything a user typed: names, messages, addresses |
| `{{{reset_url}}}` | The value exactly as given | HTML snippets and URLs you build yourself |
| `{{first_name\|there}}` | The value, or `there` if it's missing or empty | Friendly fallbacks |

Variables work in the subject, the HTML and the text version. Missing variables without a fallback become an empty string. You can also set a default fallback for each variable in the template editor.

> **Warning:** Never put user input in a `{{{triple}}}` variable. It's inserted unescaped, so someone could inject HTML into your email.

## Broadcast and automation variables

In [broadcasts](/docs/broadcasts), variables come from the contact: `{{first_name}}`, `{{last_name}}`, `{{email}}` and any [contact property](/docs/contacts), like `{{plan}}`. `{{{unsubscribe_url}}}` inserts the recipient's unsubscribe link.

In [automations](/docs/automations), templates can also use the data sent with the triggering event.

## List and fetch

- `GET /templates` lists templates with their alias and status.
- `GET /templates/:id` (id or alias) returns one template.
- `PATCH /templates/:id` changes its name, alias, sender, subject, variables or `html`. Changes are saved as a draft: emails keep using the published version until you call `POST /templates/:id/publish` again.
- `POST /templates/:id/duplicate` copies it as a new draft, and `DELETE /templates/:id` deletes it.


---

# AI writing

Write emails with AI in Delivrie's editor: draft from a web page or a brief in your brand voice, rewrite selected blocks, get subject lines, and let agents like Claude edit an email live while you watch.

The email editor for [broadcasts](/docs/broadcasts) and [templates](/docs/templates) can write with you. Open an email and choose **AI** in the top bar.

## Write from a page or a brief

Choose **Write from a page** and paste a link to a blog post, changelog, product or event page. Delivrie reads the page and writes an email from its facts, links and images. Or choose **Write from a brief** and say what the email is for. You can give both, plus a length and a tone.

The draft replaces the email's content but keeps your logo and, in broadcasts, your unsubscribe footer. Buttons use your [brand kit](https://delivrie.io/settings/brand) colour. Everything stays editable, and **Undo** puts back what was there before.

The AI only uses links and facts from the page or your brief. Check prices, dates and links before you send: the draft notes anything worth a second look.

## Rewrite blocks

Select a block and choose the sparkle button in the side panel, or **AI → Rewrite**. Shift-click to select several blocks, or select none to rewrite the whole email. Pick **Shorter**, **Clearer**, **Friendlier**, **More formal**, **Punchier** or **Fix grammar**, or type your own instruction, like "add a line about the free trial". Variables like `{{first_name}}`, links and block styles are kept.

**AI → Suggest subject lines** gives five subject lines (with preview text for broadcasts) based on what the email says.

## Brand voice

In [Settings → Brand voice](https://delivrie.io/settings/brand-voice), describe how your company writes: tone, sentence length, words you use and avoid, who your readers are. Or enter your website and choose **Suggest from website**. Every draft, rewrite and subject line follows it. Team admins can change it.

## Let agents edit live

An agent connected to the [MCP server](/docs/mcp) (Claude, Cursor, Codex, ChatGPT and others) can edit a template or draft broadcast while you have it open. Its changes appear in the editor within a few seconds, highlighted, with its name in the top bar and a note on what it changed. **Undo** reverts them. If you're in the middle of typing, Delivrie asks before loading them.

The agent uses two tools: `get_email_content` to read the blocks with their ids, and `edit_email_content` to change them one at a time. Try:

```text
Open my Delivrie broadcast "November update" and make the intro friendlier.
Add a callout after the first paragraph about the Black Friday discount (20% off Pro until Dec 1).
Keep everything else.
```

`ai_draft_email` lets an agent use Delivrie's AI writer too, optionally writing straight into an email with `target`.

## API

| Request | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /ai/draft` | Write an email from `url` and/or `brief`. Optional `kind` (`broadcast` or `template`), `length` (`short`, `medium`, `long`), `tone`, `variables`, and `target: { type, id }` to write it into a template or draft broadcast |
| `POST /ai/rewrite` | Rewrite `blocks` with an `instruction` |
| `POST /ai/subjects` | Subject line ideas for an email's `text` |
| `GET` / `PUT /ai/voice` | Read or set the brand voice (`{ "voice": "…" }`) |
| `GET /templates/:id/content`, `GET /broadcasts/:id/content` | An email's subject and blocks with ids |
| `POST /templates/:id/content`, `POST /broadcasts/:id/content` | Edit it: `ops`, or `blocks` to replace them all, plus `subject`, `preview_text` and a `summary` shown in the editor |

Each op is one of:

```json
{ "op": "replace", "id": "b3", "block": { "type": "text", "html": "New paragraph" } }
{ "op": "update", "id": "b3", "set": { "html": "Changed text" } }
{ "op": "insert", "after": "b3", "block": { "type": "button", "text": "Read more", "href": "https://acme.com/blog" } }
{ "op": "delete", "id": "b4" }
{ "op": "move", "id": "b5", "before": "b2" }
```

`after: null` inserts at the top. Block types: `title`, `heading`, `eyebrow`, `text`, `bulleted`, `numbered`, `callout`, `button`, `image`, `rows`, `divider`, `spacer`, `otp` (templates) and `footer` (broadcasts). Text fields take inline HTML: `<b>`, `<i>`, `<u>`, `<a href>` and `<br>`. Template edits are saved as a draft until you publish.

## Limits

AI writing requests (drafts, rewrites, subject lines and brand voice suggestions) a month: Free 30, Starter 300, Pro 1,000, Scale 3,000, Enterprise unlimited. Edits through `edit_email_content` and the content API don't count.


---

# Test addresses

Test deliveries, bounces, complaints and suppressions with Delivrie's test addresses, without risking your sender reputation.

Send to these addresses to test your integration end to end. They go through the full pipeline, so you get real statuses and real [webhook](/docs/webhooks) events, but no real inbox receives them and they never hurt your reputation.

| Address | What happens | Events you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delivered@test.delivrie.io` | Accepted and delivered | `email.sent`, `email.delivered` |
| `bounced@test.delivrie.io` | Rejected as a hard bounce | `email.sent`, `email.bounced` |
| `complained@test.delivrie.io` | Delivered, then marked as spam | `email.sent`, `email.delivered`, `email.complained` |
| `suppressed@test.delivrie.io` | Rejected as if on the provider's suppression list | `email.sent`, `email.bounced` |

Use the addresses exactly as written. Variations like `delivered+signup@test.delivrie.io` aren't test addresses and would be sent for real.

## Who can send to them

Send from a verified domain, or from the shared sender `onboarding@delivrie.io` before you've verified one.

## Things to know

- Test sends count toward your plan's allowance like any other email.
- Bounces and complaints from test addresses are **not** added to your suppression list, so you can repeat tests.
- Use them in CI: they give you a real round trip (send, then webhook) without emailing anyone.

```ts
// A test that checks your bounce handling end to end
await delivrie.emails.send({
  from: "Acme <onboarding@delivrie.io>",
  to: "bounced@test.delivrie.io",
  subject: "Bounce test",
  text: "This should bounce.",
});
// Your webhook endpoint should receive email.bounced within a few seconds.
```


---

# Statuses and events

What each email status means (queued, sent, delivered, bounced, complained and more), how to read an email's event history, and how statuses map to webhook events.

Every email has a status (`last_event` in the API) and a history of events. Check them in [Emails](https://delivrie.io/emails), with `GET /emails/:id`, or as they happen with [webhooks](/docs/webhooks).

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning | Final? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scheduled` | Waiting for its `scheduled_at` time | No |
| `queued` | Accepted and about to be handed to the mail servers | No |
| `sent` | Delivrie's mail servers accepted it and are delivering it | No |
| `delivery_delayed` | The recipient's server is temporarily refusing it; Delivrie keeps retrying | No |
| `delivered` | The recipient's mail server accepted it | Yes, unless opened or clicked later |
| `opened` | The recipient opened it (needs open tracking on the domain) | |
| `clicked` | The recipient clicked a link (needs click tracking on the domain) | |
| `bounced` | The recipient's server rejected it | Yes |
| `complained` | The recipient marked it as spam | Yes |
| `failed` | It couldn't be sent, for example because the domain stopped being verified. `error` says why | Yes |
| `canceled` | A scheduled email you canceled | Yes |
| `suppressed` | Every recipient was on your [suppression list](/docs/suppressions), so nothing was sent | Yes |

`delivered` means the receiving server accepted the message. Whether it lands in the inbox or spam folder is up to the receiving provider; the [Deliverability guide](/docs/deliverability) covers how to stay in the inbox.

## Event history

`GET /emails/:id` returns the email with every event:

```json
{
  "object": "email",
  "id": "4ef9a417-02e9-4d39-ad75-9611e0fcc33c",
  "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
  "to": ["ada@example.com"],
  "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
  "last_event": "delivered",
  "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:04Z",
  "events": [
    { "type": "sent", "data": { "message_id": "0102019..." }, "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:05Z" },
    { "type": "delivered", "data": { "smtp_response": "250 2.0.0 OK", "latency_ms": 812 }, "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:06Z" }
  ]
}
```

Bounce events include the type (`Permanent` or `Transient`), the sub-type and the receiving server's message, which usually says exactly why: a mailbox that doesn't exist, a full inbox, or a blocked sender.

## Bounces and complaints

- A **permanent bounce** (the address doesn't exist) adds the address to your suppression list, so you don't send to it again.
- A **transient bounce** (mailbox full, server busy) doesn't suppress the address.
- A **complaint** suppresses the address and unsubscribes the contact from broadcasts.

## Webhook events

| Status | Webhook event |
| --- | --- |
| `sent` | `email.sent` |
| `delivered` | `email.delivered` |
| `delivery_delayed` | `email.delivery_delayed` |
| `opened` | `email.opened` |
| `clicked` | `email.clicked` |
| `bounced` | `email.bounced` |
| `complained` | `email.complained` |
| `failed` | `email.failed` |

## Retention

After 30 days, an email's HTML, text and attachments are deleted. Its recipients, subject, status and events stay, so logs and metrics keep working.

Email content is kept for 30 days on every plan, for both sent and received email. Enterprise plans can keep it longer.

Use webhooks to keep your own copy if you need it longer.


---

# Errors

Every Delivrie API error, what causes it and how to fix it, with the JSON error format and which errors are safe to retry.

Errors use standard HTTP status codes and a JSON body:

```json
{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "name": "validation_error",
  "message": "The from domain mail.acme.com is not verified yet (status: pending)."
}
```

Branch on `name` in code and show `message` to people: it's written to say exactly what went wrong. Every request, including failed ones, appears in [Logs](https://delivrie.io/logs) with its request and response bodies.

## Error reference

| Status | `name` | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No `Authorization` header | Add `Authorization: Bearer dlv_...` |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | The key doesn't exist or was deleted | Check the key; create a new one in [API keys](https://delivrie.io/api-keys) |
| 403 | `restricted_api_key` | A sending-only key called another endpoint, or sent from a domain it isn't allowed to use | Use a full access key, or send from the key's domain |
| 403 | `plan_limit_reached` | You've reached your plan's domain or webhook limit | Remove one, or upgrade in [Billing](https://delivrie.io/billing) |
| 403 | `sending_paused` | Sending is paused because your bounce or complaint rate went over the limit (see [Deliverability](/docs/deliverability)) | Fix the cause, then email support@delivrie.io to resume |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope` | An MCP or OAuth connection wasn't granted this scope | Reconnect and approve the scope |
| 404 | `not_found` | Nothing with that id in this team | Check the id, and that the key belongs to the right team |
| 409 | `domain_exists` | The domain is already in this team | Use the existing domain |
| 409 | `domain_in_use` | Another team owns the domain | Claim it from the Domains page if it's yours |
| 422 | `validation_error` | A field is missing or invalid, or the `from` domain isn't verified | Read `message`; it names the field |
| 429 | `daily_quota_exceeded` | Free plan: 133 emails today. Starter: 1,500 | Wait until midnight UTC, buy credits or upgrade |
| 429 | `monthly_quota_exceeded` | Free plan: 4,000 emails this month | Buy credits or upgrade |
| 429 | `spending_cap_reached` | This send would take overage past your spending cap | Raise or remove the cap in [Billing](https://delivrie.io/billing) |
| 500 | `application_error` | Something failed on our side | Retry with the same idempotency key |
| 503 | `sending_not_configured` | Sending is temporarily unavailable | Retry later; check [status](https://delivrie.io/status) |

## Common `validation_error` messages

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Request body must be valid JSON | Send a JSON body with `Content-Type: application/json` |
| Missing from / to / subject field | Add the field |
| Provide html or text | Add a body, or send a `template` |
| The from domain X is not verified | Add and verify the domain in [Domains](https://delivrie.io/domains), or fix a typo in `from` |
| X can only send to members of your team | You're using `onboarding@delivrie.io`. Verify your own domain to email anyone |
| to can have at most 50 addresses | Split the send, or use [batch sending](/docs/send-email) |
| Attachments are limited to 40 MB per email | Send a link to the file instead |
| Attachment path isn't supported yet | Send base64 `content` |
| scheduled_at must be an ISO 8601 date or a phrase... | Use `2026-12-01T09:00:00Z` or a phrase like `in 1 hour` |
| Template X has no published version | Publish the template |
| Tag names and values can only contain... | Use letters, numbers, `_` and `-` only |

## Retrying

Retry `5xx` errors and network failures with the same `Idempotency-Key`. Don't retry `4xx` errors, including quota `429`s; they won't succeed until something changes. See [Idempotency and retries](/docs/idempotency).

## Errors in the SDK

The [Node.js SDK](/docs/sdks) returns errors instead of throwing: `const { data, error } = await delivrie.emails.send(...)`. `error` has the same `statusCode`, `name` and `message`. Problems that never reach the API have `statusCode: 0` and the name `network_error`, `timeout` or `aborted`.


---

# CORS and browser apps

Why you shouldn't call the Delivrie API from the browser, and how to send email from React, Vue, mobile and no-code front ends through a small server route instead.

If you call `https://delivrie.io/api` from code that runs in a browser or mobile app, anyone can open developer tools, copy your API key and send email as you. So keep the key on a server.

## Send through a server route

Put the API call in code you control on the server, and have your front end call that:

```ts app/api/contact/route.ts (Next.js)
import { Delivrie } from "delivrie";

const delivrie = new Delivrie(process.env.DELIVRIE_API_KEY);
```
