```ts app/api/contact/route.ts (Next.js)
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { email, message } = await req.json();
  if (!email || !message) return Response.json({ error: "Missing fields" }, { status: 400 });

  const { error } = await delivrie.emails.send({
    from: "Website <forms@mail.acme.com>",
    to: "team@acme.com",
    replyTo: email,
    subject: "New message from the website",
    text: message,
  });
  return error ? Response.json({ error: error.message }, { status: 502 }) : Response.json({ ok: true });
}
```

```ts Front end
await fetch("/api/contact", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, message }),
});
```

Good places for that server code: a Next.js route handler or Server Action, a [Supabase Edge Function](/docs/supabase), a [Cloudflare Worker](/docs/cloudflare-workers), a Vercel or Netlify function, Firebase Cloud Functions, or your own backend.

## Protect the route

A public route that sends email can be abused too. Before sending:

- Send to fixed addresses you control (like your team inbox) rather than an address from the request, or only to the signed-in user's own address.
- Rate-limit by IP or user.
- Add a CAPTCHA (Turnstile, hCaptcha or reCAPTCHA) to public forms.
- Use a [sending access key](/docs/api-keys) limited to one domain.

## No-code and AI app builders

Lovable, Bolt, v0, Replit and similar tools can generate the server route for you. Ask them to "send email from a server function using the Delivrie API, reading DELIVRIE_API_KEY from secrets, never from the browser". See [Build with AI](/docs/build-with-ai) for prompts.


---

# SMTP

Send through Delivrie's SMTP relay from WordPress, Laravel, Django, Rails, Ghost, Supabase Auth, Nodemailer and anything else that speaks SMTP.

Anything that can send over SMTP can send through Delivrie: CMSs, frameworks, no-code tools, printers and legacy apps. SMTP mail gets the same limits, logs, webhooks and suppressions as the API.

## Settings

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Host | `smtp.delivrie.io` |
| Port | `587` with STARTTLS, or `465` with SSL/TLS |
| Alternative ports | `2587` (STARTTLS) and `2465` (SSL/TLS), for hosts that block the usual ones |
| Username | `delivrie` |
| Password | A Delivrie API key (`dlv_...`). A sending access key is enough |
| Encryption | Required. On 587 choose STARTTLS (sometimes called TLS); on 465 choose SSL/TLS (sometimes called SSL or SMTPS) |

The `From` address must be on a verified domain, the same as with the API.

## Examples

```js Nodemailer
const transport = nodemailer.createTransport({
  host: "smtp.delivrie.io",
  port: 587,
  secure: false, // upgrades with STARTTLS
  auth: { user: "delivrie", pass: process.env.DELIVRIE_API_KEY },
});
```

```bash Laravel .env
MAIL_MAILER=smtp
MAIL_HOST=smtp.delivrie.io
MAIL_PORT=587
MAIL_ENCRYPTION=tls
MAIL_USERNAME=delivrie
MAIL_PASSWORD=dlv_your_key
```

```python Django
EMAIL_HOST = "smtp.delivrie.io"
EMAIL_PORT = 587
EMAIL_USE_TLS = True
EMAIL_HOST_USER = "delivrie"
EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD = os.environ["DELIVRIE_API_KEY"]
```

```ruby Rails
config.action_mailer.smtp_settings = {
  address: "smtp.delivrie.io", port: 587, user_name: "delivrie",
  password: ENV.fetch("DELIVRIE_API_KEY"), authentication: :plain, enable_starttls_auto: true,
}
```

```bash swaks (testing)
swaks --server smtp.delivrie.io:587 --tls \
  --auth-user delivrie --auth-password "$DELIVRIE_API_KEY" \
  --from hello@mail.acme.com --to delivered@test.delivrie.io
```

Step-by-step setup for [Supabase Auth](/docs/supabase), [WordPress and Laravel](/docs/php), [Django](/docs/python) and [Rails](/docs/ruby) is in their guides.

## What's supported

- To, Cc and Bcc come from the message and the SMTP envelope.
- Attachments are kept, up to 40 MB per message.
- Custom `X-` headers and `List-Unsubscribe` are passed through.
- Tag a message with an `X-Delivrie-Tags` header: `X-Delivrie-Tags: source=wordpress, order`. Tags appear in the dashboard and in webhook events.
- Each message is sent once even if your app retries, based on its `Message-ID`.

## SMTP replies

| Reply | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `535` | Authentication failed | The username must be `delivrie` and the password a valid API key |
| `550` | The API rejected the message | The reply says why, for example an unverified From domain |
| `452` | A sending limit was reached | Retry later, or check your plan in [Billing](https://delivrie.io/billing) |

After five failed logins from one IP address, logins from that address are blocked for 15 minutes.

## Troubleshooting connections

- **Timeouts:** some hosts (DigitalOcean, Google Cloud, some home ISPs) block outbound ports 25, 465 and 587. Use port `2587` or `2465`.
- **TLS errors on 465:** your client is trying STARTTLS on an SSL port. Choose SSL/TLS, or switch to 587.
- **"Must issue a STARTTLS command first":** turn on encryption. Plain-text logins aren't accepted.


---

# Receiving email

Receive email on your domain with Delivrie: set up the MX record, choose which addresses accept mail, get email.received webhooks, read messages with the API and forward them automatically to Gmail or any inbox.

Delivrie can receive email for your domain: replies to your app's emails, a `support@` address, inbound parsing for tickets or uploads. Every received message is stored, sent to your webhooks as `email.received`, and grouped into conversations in the [Inbox](/docs/inbox).

## Set it up

1. Open your domain in [Domains](https://delivrie.io/domains) and turn on **Receiving**.
2. Pick where mail arrives:
   - **A subdomain** such as `in.acme.com` (recommended). Your normal email at `acme.com`, like Google Workspace, keeps working.
   - **The domain itself.** Only do this if nothing else receives mail for it, because its MX record will point at Delivrie.
3. Choose which addresses accept mail: **all addresses** (`anything@in.acme.com`) or **only specific addresses** (mail to anything else is dropped).
4. Add the `MX` record Delivrie shows, priority `10`, and click **Verify DNS records**.

> **Warning:** Adding Delivrie's MX record to a domain that already receives mail elsewhere (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Zoho) sends that mail to Delivrie instead. Use a subdomain unless you mean to move your inbox.

You can also configure receiving with [`PATCH /domains/:id`](/docs/api/update-domain):

```json
{
  "receiving_enabled": true,
  "receiving_subdomain": "in",
  "receiving_mode": "specific",
  "receiving_addresses": ["support@in.acme.com", "billing@in.acme.com"]
}
```

## Get received mail as a webhook

Add a [webhook](/docs/webhooks) subscribed to `email.received`:

```json
{
  "type": "email.received",
  "created_at": "2026-11-14T10:22:31.000Z",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "a5c3e1f0-...",
    "from": "Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>",
    "to": ["support@in.acme.com"],
    "subject": "Re: Your order is confirmed",
    "created_at": "2026-11-14T10:22:30.000Z",
    "message_id": "<CAF=abc123@mail.gmail.com>",
    "attachments": [{ "filename": "photo.jpg", "content_type": "image/jpeg", "size": 248213 }]
  }
}
```

Fetch the full message, with its HTML and text, using `GET /emails/:email_id`.

## Read received mail with the API

```bash
# Newest first; filter by the address it was sent to
curl "https://delivrie.io/api/emails/received?to=support@in.acme.com&limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"
```

`GET /emails?direction=inbound` lists received mail too.

Download attachments with `GET /emails/received/:id/attachments`. Each file comes with a `download_url` that works for an hour:

```json
{ "object": "list", "data": [{ "object": "attachment", "id": "att_1", "filename": "photo.jpg", "content_type": "image/jpeg", "size": 248213, "download_url": "https://…", "expires_at": "2026-11-28T11:22:30Z" }] }
```

## Reply and forward

- **Reply** from the [Inbox](/docs/inbox), or with `POST /inbox/threads/:id/reply`. Delivrie sets `In-Reply-To` and `References`, so the reply lands in the same conversation in the sender's mail app.
- **Forward** a received email with `POST /emails/:id/forward` and `{ "to": "ops@acme.com", "from": "Acme <support@mail.acme.com>" }`.

## Forward received mail to Gmail or another inbox

Delivrie doesn't offer IMAP or POP3, so a mail app can't connect to it directly. Instead, turn on **Forward a copy** on the domain's Receiving page and every email the domain receives is also sent to the inboxes you choose, up to 5.

```json
{ "receiving_forward_to": ["you@gmail.com"] }
```

Send that to [`PATCH /domains/:id`](/docs/api/update-domain). An empty list turns forwarding off.

- The copy is sent **from the address that received it** (for example `support@in.acme.com`), shown as "Ada Lovelace via acme.com", so it passes SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
- **Reply-To is the original sender**, so replying from Gmail goes straight to them. To reply *as* your address from Gmail, add it under Gmail's "Send mail as" with Delivrie's [SMTP settings](/docs/smtp).
- Attachments are included, up to 10 MB in total.
- Each forward counts as one sent email and appears in **Emails** with the tag `auto_forward`.
- Messages flagged as spam or carrying a virus aren't forwarded, and the domain must be verified for sending.
- The email still arrives in Delivrie: the Inbox, the API and `email.received` webhooks work as before.

## Make your app's emails replyable

Set `reply_to` to a receiving address when you send, and customer replies come back to Delivrie:

```json
{ "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>", "reply_to": "support@in.acme.com", "to": "ada@example.com", "subject": "Your order is confirmed", "html": "..." }
```

## How long received mail is kept

Received email and Inbox replies are kept for 30 days on every plan. After that the message body and attachments are deleted; the sender, subject and thread stay. Save anything you need longer from the `email.received` webhook.

## Spam and security checks

Each received email's `received` event records the receiving server's spam, virus, SPF, DKIM and DMARC verdicts. Check them before acting on mail automatically, especially for messages that trigger actions in your app.


---

# Inbox

Inboxes for people and agents: an inbox per address, an agent that drafts replies, labels and filters spam, shared drafts, internal notes, assignment, Gmail-style search, and the API and MCP tools behind them.

The [Inbox](https://delivrie.io/inbox) groups [received email](/docs/receiving) into conversations so your team, and an AI agent, can read, sort and answer them in one place.

## Inboxes

An inbox is an address on a receiving domain, like `support@in.acme.com` or `sales@in.acme.com`. Mail to that address lands in it. Create one from the inbox menu in the dashboard (**New inbox**) or with `POST /inboxes`. Each address that already had mail became an inbox automatically. Mail to addresses without an inbox still arrives and shows under **Other mail**.

If the domain only accepts specific addresses, creating an inbox adds its address to that list. If the domain receives on a subdomain (like `in.acme.com`), the inbox has to use an address there.

## The inbox agent

Each inbox can have an agent that reads every new email and acts on it within the limits you set. Turn it on in the inbox's settings, write instructions in plain language (what the inbox is for, your policies, links to share, who handles what), pick a tone, and choose what it may do:

| Action | What the agent does |
| --- | --- |
| Draft replies | Writes a reply in the conversation for someone to review and send. **It never sends replies itself.** |
| Add labels | Sorts conversations with your labels, creating new ones when needed |
| Mark spam | Moves scams, phishing and bulk mail to Spam |
| Archive | Files mail that needs no reply, like receipts and notifications |
| Assign | Hands the conversation to someone on your team |
| Add notes | Leaves an internal note. Notes are never emailed |
| Forward | Forwards mail, but only to the addresses you list in its settings (up to 5) |

Email is written by people outside your team, so the agent treats it as untrusted text: it only has the actions you allowed, it can't forward anywhere you didn't list, and it ignores instructions inside an email that try to change what it does. Every run is logged with what it did, shown at the top of the conversation and in the inbox's settings. You can also run it on any conversation from the thread's menu (**Run agent**) or with `POST /inbox/threads/:id/agent`.

Agent runs a month, across all inboxes: Free 100, Starter 1,000, Pro 3,000, Scale 10,000, Enterprise unlimited.

## Conversations

A message joins an existing thread when it replies to an earlier message (its `In-Reply-To` or `References` header points at one), or when the same person writes to the same address with the same subject within 30 days. Otherwise it starts a new thread. Replies you send from the Inbox join their thread with the right headers, so they stay in the same conversation in the customer's mail app.

Each thread has an inbox, a contact, a subject, a snippet, unread status, labels, an assignee and a folder: `open`, `archived`, `spam` or `trash`. `needs_reply` is `true` when the latest message is from the contact. A new conversation that the receiving server flags as spam starts in Spam.

- **Drafts** are shared by the team. A reply you start in the dashboard saves as you type, so a teammate can pick it up. The agent's drafts appear in the reply box with its note on what to check.
- **Notes** are internal comments on a conversation, from your team or the agent. They're never emailed.
- **Assignment** gives a conversation an owner. **Assigned to me** lists yours.

## Search

The search box and the API's `q` parameter take Gmail-style syntax. Combine as many as you like:

| Example | Finds |
| --- | --- |
| `refund "charged twice"` | Words and exact phrases in the subject, contact or latest message |
| `from:maria` `to:sales@` `subject:invoice` | Sender, the inbox address, or the subject |
| `label:billing` | Conversations with that label |
| `is:unread` `is:read` `is:assigned` `is:unassigned` `is:needs-reply` | Status |
| `in:archive` `in:spam` `in:trash` `in:anywhere` | A folder other than the open inbox |
| `has:attachment` `has:draft` | Conversations with attachments, or with an open draft |
| `after:2026-11-01` `before:2026-12-01` | By the latest message's date |

## API

| Request | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /inboxes` | List inboxes with open, unread and needs-reply counts and their agent settings |
| `POST /inboxes` | Create an inbox: `{ "address": "support@in.acme.com", "name": "Support" }` |
| `PATCH /inboxes/:id` | Change `name`, `description` or `agent` (see below). `:id` can be the inbox's id or address |
| `DELETE /inboxes/:id` | Remove an inbox. Its conversations move to Other mail |
| `GET /inboxes/:id/agent-runs` | The agent's recent runs, with what it did |
| `GET /inbox/threads` | List threads, newest first. Filters: `inbox` (id, address or `none`), `status` (`open`, the default, `archived`, `spam`, `trash` or `all`), `unread=true`, `needs_reply=true`, `assignee` (`me`, an email or `none`), `label`, `q` (search syntax above), `limit` |
| `GET /inbox/threads/:id` | A thread with its messages as text, notes, open drafts and recent agent runs |
| `POST /inbox/threads/:id/reply` | Reply with `{ "text": "..." }` or `{ "html": "..." }`. Optional `from`, `cc`, and `draft_id` to mark a draft as sent |
| `PATCH /inbox/threads/:id` | Change `status`, `unread`, `assignee` (an email, `me` or `null`) or `labels` (names; new labels are created) |
| `POST /inbox/threads/:id/agent` | Run the inbox's agent on this conversation now |
| `GET` / `POST /inbox/threads/:id/notes` | List notes, or add one with `{ "body": "..." }` |
| `DELETE /inbox/notes/:id` | Delete a note |
| `GET /inbox/drafts` | Open drafts. Filters: `thread_id`, `inbox`, `source` (`user` or `agent`) |
| `POST /inbox/drafts` | Save a draft: a reply with `thread_id`, or a new email with `inbox`; plus `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `text` or `html` |
| `PATCH /inbox/drafts/:id` | Edit a draft |
| `POST /inbox/drafts/:id/send` | Send a draft (replies keep their threading) |
| `DELETE /inbox/drafts/:id` | Discard a draft |
| `GET /inbox/labels` | List labels |

The `agent` object: `enabled` (boolean), `instructions` (up to 4,000 characters), `tone` (`friendly`, `professional`, `concise` or your own words), `actions` (any of `draft_reply`, `add_labels`, `archive`, `mark_spam`, `assign`, `add_note`, `forward`), `forward_to` (up to 5 addresses, required for `forward`) and `signature`. Changing inboxes and their agent needs a full access key, or the `manage` scope for connected apps.

```bash
# Turn on the agent for the support inbox
curl -X PATCH https://delivrie.io/api/inboxes/support@in.acme.com \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "agent": { "enabled": true, "instructions": "We sell Acme Projects. Refunds within 30 days of purchase. Billing questions go to Sam.", "actions": ["draft_reply", "add_labels", "mark_spam", "assign"] } }'

# Unread billing conversations that need an answer
curl -G "https://delivrie.io/api/inbox/threads" --data-urlencode "q=label:billing is:unread is:needs-reply" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"

# Send the agent's draft after checking it
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/inbox/drafts/DRAFT_ID/send -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"
```

The Inbox has its own [webhook events](/docs/webhooks): `inbox.email.received`, `inbox.email.sent`, `inbox.thread.updated`, `inbox.draft.created`, `inbox.draft.sent`, `inbox.draft.discarded`, `inbox.note.created`, `inbox.agent.completed`, `inbox.agent.failed`, and `inbox.created`, `inbox.updated` and `inbox.deleted`.

## Work the Inbox from your own agent

Connect an assistant to the [MCP server](/docs/mcp) and it can use the same features: `list_inboxes`, `list_inbox_threads` (with search), `get_inbox_thread`, `create_draft`, `send_draft`, `reply_to_thread`, `update_thread`, `add_thread_note`, `run_inbox_agent` and `update_inbox`. For example, in Claude:

```text
Check the support inbox in Delivrie for conversations that need a reply.
For each one, read it and save a draft answer using our refund policy (below).
Don't send anything: I'll review the drafts. Label each one "billing" or "bug".
```

Approve the `read` and `send` scopes, and leave out `manage`, if the agent should read, draft and reply but not change inbox settings.


---

# Domains and DNS

Add and verify a sending domain: which DNS records Delivrie needs (DKIM, SPF return path, DMARC, MX for receiving), how to enter them at common DNS providers, tracking and TLS settings.

To send from your own address, add the domain to Delivrie and publish a few DNS records that prove you own it and let mailbox providers trust your mail.

## Use a subdomain

Send from a subdomain such as `mail.acme.com` or `notify.acme.com` rather than `acme.com`. Your app's email then builds its own reputation, and a problem with it can't affect the mail your team sends from `acme.com`. Customers still see whatever `from` name and address you choose, like `Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>`.

## Add the domain

In [Domains](https://delivrie.io/domains/new), enter the domain and click **Add domain**. Or with the API:

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/domains \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "mail.acme.com" }'
```

The response lists the records to add. Options: `return_path` (bounce subdomain, default `send`), `open_tracking` and `click_tracking` (both off by default). Mail is sent from Ireland (`eu-west-1`).

## The DNS records

For `mail.acme.com`, you'll see records like these:

| Purpose | Type | Name | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DKIM (signs your mail) | `TXT` | `<selector>._domainkey.mail.acme.com` | `p=MIGfMA0GCSq...` (your public key) |
| Return path: bounces | `MX` | `send.mail.acme.com` | `feedback-smtp.eu-west-1.amazonses.com`, priority `10` |
| Return path: SPF | `TXT` | `send.mail.acme.com` | `v=spf1 include:_spf.delivrie.io ~all` |
| DMARC (recommended) | `TXT` | `_dmarc.mail.acme.com` | `v=DMARC1; p=none;` |
| Receiving (optional) | `MX` | `mail.acme.com` or your receiving subdomain | `inbound-smtp.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com`, priority `10` |

The `feedback-smtp...amazonses.com` and `inbound-smtp...amazonaws.com` hosts belong to Delivrie's mail infrastructure. Use the exact values from your dashboard; the DKIM key is unique to your domain. **Copy records as text** in the domain's menu gives you all of them at once.

## Set up automatically on Cloudflare

If your domain's DNS is on Cloudflare, Delivrie can add the records for you:

1. Open the domain and click **Set up with Cloudflare**.
2. Click **Create a Cloudflare token**. Cloudflare opens with the permissions filled in (**Zone: Read** and **DNS: Edit**). Under **Zone Resources**, pick the specific zone for your domain, create the token and copy it.
3. Paste the token and click **Add records**.

Delivrie uses the token once and doesn't keep it, and it's blanked out of your request logs. You can delete the token in Cloudflare afterwards.

Records are only ever **added**. Nothing already in your DNS is changed or deleted:

- A record that's already there with the same value is left as it is.
- If the name already has an SPF record, it's flagged so you can merge ours into it by hand (a name can only have one).
- If the domain already has a DMARC policy, yours is kept.
- If the name already has an MX record from another mail service, it's flagged and left alone, so your existing email keeps working.

You can do the same with the API: `POST /domains/:id/cloudflare` with `{ "api_token": "…" }` returns the domain plus a `cloudflare` object listing the records `created`, `existing` and `skipped` (with the reason).

## Entering records at your DNS provider

Most providers add your root domain to the name automatically. If your DNS zone is `acme.com`, enter only the part before it:

| Full name | What to type in the Name / Host field |
| --- | --- |
| `<selector>._domainkey.mail.acme.com` | `<selector>._domainkey.mail` |
| `send.mail.acme.com` | `send.mail` |
| `_dmarc.mail.acme.com` | `_dmarc.mail` |

Provider notes:

- **Cloudflare:** set every record to **DNS only** (grey cloud). MX and TXT records can't be proxied anyway.
- **GoDaddy, Namecheap, Hostinger:** use the short names above. Namecheap lists MX records under **Mail Settings → Custom MX**.
- **Route 53, Google Cloud DNS:** enter the full name, and wrap TXT values in double quotes.
- **Vercel DNS:** enter the short name; Vercel adds the domain.

## Verify

Click **Verify DNS records** (or `POST /domains/:id/verify`). Each record shows its own status. Most providers update within minutes; some take up to 72 hours. Delivrie also re-checks pending domains in the background and sends a `domain.updated` webhook when the status changes.

Statuses: `not_started` (records not found yet), `pending` (some found), `verified` (ready to send), `failed` or `temporary_failure` (a record was found but is wrong; fix it and verify again).

Stuck? See [Why isn't my domain verifying?](/docs/domain-not-verifying)

## Settings

Change these on the domain's page or with `PATCH /domains/:id`:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `open_tracking` | Adds an invisible image to count opens. Off by default |
| `click_tracking` | Rewrites links to count clicks. Off by default |
| `tls` | `opportunistic` (default) uses TLS when the receiving server supports it; `enforced` only delivers over TLS |
| `return_path` | The bounce subdomain label, default `send`. Changing it gives you new SPF records to add |

> **Note:** Open tracking is approximate. Apple Mail and some corporate filters load images automatically, which counts as an open even if nobody read the email.

## Several domains, several teams

Each domain belongs to one team. To use the same domain in another team, delete it from the first, or start a **claim** from the other team's Domains page, which proves ownership with a DNS record and moves it.


---

# Why isn't my domain verifying?

Fix a Delivrie domain stuck on pending or failed: doubled record names, split DKIM values, duplicate SPF records, Cloudflare proxying, propagation, and how to check DNS yourself.

Work through these in order. Most stuck domains have one of the first three problems.

## 1. The record name is doubled

Many DNS providers add your domain to the end of the name. If you type the full name, you get `<selector>._domainkey.mail.acme.com.acme.com`.

Fix: type only the part before your root domain, like `<selector>._domainkey.mail`. See [Entering records at your DNS provider](/docs/domains).

## 2. The DKIM value was changed

The DKIM `TXT` value is long. Some providers split it or add quotes or spaces.

Fix: paste the whole value, starting with `p=`, as a single string. If your provider needs long values split, split it into quoted chunks with no spaces inside the key.

## 3. Two SPF records on the same name

A name can only have one SPF (`v=spf1`) record. If `send.mail.acme.com` already has one, from Resend or another provider, the check fails.

Fix: delete the old record, or set a different return path in the domain's settings (for example `bounces`) and add the new SPF records there.

## 4. Cloudflare is proxying

Records set to **Proxied** (orange cloud) don't resolve as written.

Fix: switch each Delivrie record to **DNS only** (grey cloud).

## 5. DNS hasn't updated yet

Changes usually show up within minutes, but some providers take hours, and up to 72 hours in rare cases.

Fix: wait, then click **Verify DNS records**. Delivrie also keeps checking pending domains in the background, and sends a `domain.updated` webhook when the status changes.

## Check DNS yourself

Look the records up from your computer:

```bash
dig +short TXT <selector>._domainkey.mail.acme.com
dig +short MX send.mail.acme.com
dig +short TXT send.mail.acme.com
```

Or use a web tool such as [Google's dig](https://toolbox.googleapps.com/apps/dig/). If the answer is empty, the record isn't live yet or the name is wrong. If it shows a different value, fix the value.

Still stuck after checking all of these? Use the chat button in the dashboard, and include the domain name. We'll look at your DNS with you.


---

# DMARC

Set up DMARC for your sending domain, roll it out safely from p=none to p=reject, and meet Gmail and Yahoo's bulk sender requirements.

DMARC tells mailbox providers what to do with mail that claims to be from your domain but fails SPF and DKIM checks, and where to send reports about it. Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft require it for bulk senders, and it helps everyone else reach the inbox.

## Add the record

Add a `TXT` record at `_dmarc` on your sending domain (for `mail.acme.com`, the name is `_dmarc.mail.acme.com`):

```text
v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@acme.com
```

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `p` | Policy: `none` (monitor only), `quarantine` (send failures to spam) or `reject` (block failures) |
| `rua` | Where providers send daily aggregate reports |
| `pct` | Optional: apply the policy to this percentage of failing mail, for gradual rollout |

If your root domain (`acme.com`) already has a DMARC record, it covers subdomains too, unless the subdomain has its own.

## Roll it out

1. Start with `p=none` and collect reports for two to four weeks. A free report reader (Postmark's DMARC tool, dmarcian, EasyDMARC) turns the XML into something readable.
2. Check that everything sending as your domain passes: Delivrie, your workspace email, your CRM, your helpdesk. Set up DKIM for any that fail.
3. Move to `p=quarantine`, optionally with `pct=25` at first.
4. Finish at `p=reject`.

Mail sent through Delivrie from a verified domain passes DMARC: it's DKIM-signed with your domain, and the return path on your domain passes SPF.

## Gmail and Yahoo requirements

If you send more than 5,000 emails a day to Gmail or Yahoo addresses, they require:

- SPF and DKIM (Delivrie sets both up when you verify the domain)
- a DMARC record, at least `p=none`
- one-click unsubscribe on marketing email (Delivrie adds it to [broadcasts](/docs/broadcasts) automatically)
- a spam complaint rate under 0.3%; aim for under 0.1%

See the [Deliverability guide](/docs/deliverability) for the rest.


---

# Deliverability guide

How to keep Delivrie email out of spam: authentication, warming up a new domain, bounce and complaint thresholds, content, list hygiene and what to do when mail goes to spam.

Deliverability is whether your email reaches the inbox rather than the spam folder. Mailbox providers decide based on your domain's authentication, your sending history and how recipients react.

## The basics

1. **Authenticate.** Verify your domain so mail is DKIM-signed and passes SPF, and add [DMARC](/docs/dmarc).
2. **Send from a subdomain** like `mail.acme.com`, so app email and team email don't share a reputation.
3. **Only email people who asked for it.** Never buy or scrape lists.
4. **Make unsubscribing easy.** Broadcasts get a one-click unsubscribe header automatically; include a visible link too.
5. **Send what people expect,** when they expect it. Password resets and receipts rarely go to spam; surprise newsletters do.

## Stay under these limits

| Metric | Keep it under | What happens above it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bounce rate | 4% | Providers start blocking you, and Delivrie pauses your sending |
| Complaint rate | 0.08% (and never above 0.3%) | Gmail and Yahoo filter or reject your mail, and Delivrie pauses your sending |

### Automatic pause

Delivrie checks every account once an hour. If, over the last 7 days, more than 4% of your emails bounced (once you've sent at least 100) or more than 0.08% were marked as spam (once you've sent at least 1,000), sending is paused for the whole account. Sends then fail with `403 sending_paused`, and your team admins get an email explaining why. Emails to the [test addresses](/docs/test-mode) don't count.

To resume, find the cause (usually an old or imported list, or a sign-up form without validation), remove the bad addresses, and email support@delivrie.io with what you changed. This protects your domain's reputation as well as everyone else's.

Watch both in [Metrics](https://delivrie.io/metrics) or with `GET /metrics`.

## Warm up a new domain

A new domain has no reputation. Start with your most-engaged recipients and grow over a few weeks:

| Week | Emails a day |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Up to a few hundred |
| 2 | 1,000 to 2,000 |
| 3 | 5,000 |
| 4 onward | Double while bounces and complaints stay low |

Transactional email (sign-ins, receipts) warms a domain naturally, because people open it.

## Keep your list clean

- Confirm addresses at sign-up (double opt-in for newsletters).
- Delivrie adds hard bounces and complaints to your [suppression list](/docs/suppressions) automatically. Don't remove addresses from it unless you're sure they're valid.
- Remove contacts who haven't opened anything in six months, or ask them to re-confirm.
- Use [test addresses](/docs/test-mode) for testing, never made-up addresses at real domains.

## Content

- Send a plain-text part (Delivrie generates one from your HTML).
- Keep a sensible balance of text and images; never send a single image as the whole email.
- Use your real domain in links. Link shorteners and mismatched domains look like phishing.
- Avoid misleading subject lines, all caps and lots of exclamation marks.
- Keep the HTML under about 100 KB; Gmail clips larger messages.

## If mail goes to spam

1. Check the email's events in [Emails](https://delivrie.io/emails). `delivered` means the provider accepted it; where it filed it is the provider's choice.
2. Check that SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass: in Gmail, open the message, choose **Show original** and look for `PASS` on all three.
3. Look at recent bounce and complaint rates in [Metrics](https://delivrie.io/metrics).
4. Register your domain with [Google Postmaster Tools](https://postmaster.google.com) to see your reputation at Gmail.
5. If you changed something recently (a new domain, a bigger list, new content), go back to sending only to engaged recipients for a week or two.


---

# Dedicated IPs

Send from IP addresses only your team uses, warmed up and scaled automatically. Available on Scale and Enterprise.

By default, Delivrie sends your mail from a shared pool of IP addresses with a strong reputation. With dedicated IPs, your mail goes out from addresses only your team uses, so your sending reputation depends only on what you send.

Dedicated IPs are available on the **Scale** and **Enterprise** plans. They suit senders with steady volume, usually **3,000 emails a day or more**. Below that, shared IPs give you a better reputation, and Amazon may move low-volume mail back to them anyway.

## How it works

Delivrie uses Amazon SES managed dedicated IPs. When yours are switched on:

- Each region your domains send from gets its own pool of IPs for your team, and your domains are moved onto it. Your API calls, SMTP settings and DNS records don't change.
- The IPs are **warmed up automatically**, separately for each mailbox provider (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo and so on). During warm-up, which takes a few weeks, some of your mail still goes out through the shared pool so delivery stays steady.
- More IPs are added as your volume grows, and removed if it drops for a long time.
- If you add a domain in a new region later, it gets a pool there too.

Your reputation is now yours alone, so keep bounce and complaint rates low: send only to people who asked for your mail, and remove addresses that bounce. The [deliverability guide](/docs/deliverability) covers the details.

## Get dedicated IPs

1. Go to **Settings → Dedicated IPs** (team admins only).
2. Choose **Request dedicated IPs** and tell us your expected volume.
3. We review requests within one business day. Your team's admins get an email when the IPs are on.

To turn them off, choose **Turn off dedicated IPs** on the same page. Your domains go back to the shared IPs straight away and the dedicated IPs are released. If you want them again later, they need warming up again.

## Check the status from the API

`GET /dedicated-ips` returns the status (`off`, `requested`, `active`, `declined` and so on), the regions with a pool, your plan and your average daily volume over the last 14 days. Requesting and turning them off happen in the dashboard.

```bash
curl https://delivrie.io/api/dedicated-ips -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"
```


---

# Suppression list

How Delivrie's suppression list protects your reputation: which addresses are added automatically, and how to add, list and remove addresses with the dashboard or API.

Your team's suppression list holds addresses Delivrie won't send to. Sends to a suppressed address are skipped automatically, so one bad address can't keep hurting your reputation.

## What gets added automatically

| Event | Added? |
| --- | --- |
| Hard (permanent) bounce: the address doesn't exist | Yes, reason `bounce` |
| Spam complaint | Yes, reason `complaint`. The contact is also unsubscribed from broadcasts |
| Soft (transient) bounce: mailbox full, server busy | No |
| Bounces and complaints from [test addresses](/docs/test-mode) | No |

## What happens when you send to one

Suppressed addresses are removed from `to`, `cc` and `bcc` when the email is sent, and the rest of the recipients get it as normal. If every recipient is suppressed, the email's status becomes `suppressed` and nothing is sent. The API still returns `200` with an id, so check the status or watch your webhooks if this matters to you.

## Manage the list

In the dashboard, open [Suppressions](https://delivrie.io/suppressions). With the API:

```bash
# Add one or several
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/suppressions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "email": ["old@example.com", "left@example.com"] }'

# List (up to 1,000, with the reason)
curl https://delivrie.io/api/suppressions -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"

# Remove
curl -X DELETE https://delivrie.io/api/suppressions/old@example.com -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"
```

> **Warning:** Only remove an address if you know it now works, for example the person fixed a typo or asked to receive email again. Sending to addresses that bounced or complained again damages your reputation quickly.

## Importing from another provider

Moving from another provider? Import its bounce and complaint lists with `POST /suppressions` before your first send, so you don't repeat their mistakes.


---

# Webhooks

Get Delivrie events (sent, delivered, bounced, complained, opened, clicked, received, contact and domain changes) pushed to your server, with payload examples, signature verification in every language, retries and replays.

Webhooks push events to your server as they happen, so you don't have to poll. Use them to mark bounced addresses, record deliveries, react to replies and keep your own history.

## Add an endpoint

In [Webhooks](https://delivrie.io/webhooks), click **Add endpoint**, enter an `https://` URL and choose events. Or with the API:

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "endpoint": "https://acme.com/webhooks/delivrie", "events": ["email.delivered", "email.bounced", "email.complained"] }'
```

The response includes `signing_secret` (starts with `whsec_`). It's shown once: store it as `DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Use `["*"]` to receive every event.

## Events

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `email.sent` | Delivrie's mail servers accepted the email |
| `email.delivered` | The recipient's server accepted it |
| `email.delivery_delayed` | Delivery is temporarily failing and being retried |
| `email.bounced` | The recipient's server rejected it |
| `email.complained` | The recipient marked it as spam |
| `email.opened` | Opened (open tracking must be on for the domain) |
| `email.clicked` | A link was clicked (click tracking must be on) |
| `email.failed` | It couldn't be sent; `failed.reason` says why |
| `email.received` | Mail arrived at one of your [receiving](/docs/receiving) addresses |
| `contact.created`, `contact.updated`, `contact.deleted` | A contact changed |
| `contact.import.completed` | A [contact import](/docs/contacts) finished; includes `created`, `updated`, `skipped` and up to 100 `errors` |
| `domain.created`, `domain.updated` | A domain was added or its verification status changed |
| `broadcast.created`, `broadcast.updated`, `broadcast.deleted` | A [broadcast](/docs/broadcasts) was created (including duplicates), edited or deleted through the API or dashboard |
| `broadcast.scheduled` | A broadcast was scheduled or sent now; `scheduled_at` says when it goes out and `recipients` how many it will reach |
| `broadcast.canceled` | A scheduled broadcast was canceled and moved back to drafts |
| `broadcast.sending` | Sending started; `recipients` is the final count after unsubscribes, topic opt-outs and suppressions |
| `broadcast.sent` | Every email was handed to the mail servers; `stats` has the counts so far (delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) |
| `inbox.email.received` | Mail arrived in the [Inbox](/docs/inbox): includes `thread_id`, `inbox_id` and the thread's folder (`open` or `spam`) |
| `inbox.thread.updated` | A conversation was moved, assigned, labelled or marked read; `changes` lists what changed and `by` says who (`member`, `api` or `agent`) |
| `inbox.email.sent` | Your team replied in a conversation, from the dashboard, the API, MCP or by sending a draft |
| `inbox.draft.created` | A draft was saved in a conversation; `source` is `agent` when the inbox agent wrote it |
| `inbox.draft.sent`, `inbox.draft.discarded` | A draft was sent (with the new `email_id`) or discarded |
| `inbox.note.created` | An internal note was added; `author` is `member` or `agent` |
| `inbox.agent.completed` | The inbox agent finished a run; `actions` lists what it did |
| `inbox.agent.failed` | An inbox agent run failed; `error` says why |
| `inbox.created`, `inbox.updated`, `inbox.deleted` | An inbox was added, changed (including its agent settings) or removed |

## Payloads

Every request is a `POST` with a JSON body of `{ type, created_at, data }`.

```json email.delivered
{
  "type": "email.delivered",
  "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:06.511Z",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "4ef9a417-02e9-4d39-ad75-9611e0fcc33c",
    "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
    "to": ["ada@example.com"],
    "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
    "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:04.120Z",
    "tags": { "category": "receipt" }
  }
}
```

```json email.bounced
{
  "type": "email.bounced",
  "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:07.002Z",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "4ef9a417-02e9-4d39-ad75-9611e0fcc33c",
    "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
    "to": ["nobody@example.com"],
    "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
    "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:04.120Z",
    "bounce": {
      "type": "Permanent",
      "sub_type": "General",
      "message": "smtp; 550 5.1.1 user unknown",
      "recipients": [{ "emailAddress": "nobody@example.com" }]
    }
  }
}
```

```json email.clicked
{
  "type": "email.clicked",
  "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:30:12.000Z",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "4ef9a417-...",
    "from": "Acme <orders@mail.acme.com>",
    "to": ["ada@example.com"],
    "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
    "created_at": "2026-11-14T09:12:04.120Z",
    "click": { "link": "https://acme.com/orders/1042", "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0 ...", "ip": "102.89.0.1" }
  }
}
```

```json contact.created
{
  "type": "contact.created",
  "created_at": "2026-11-14T08:00:00.000Z",
  "data": { "id": "c_12...", "email": "ada@example.com", "first_name": "Ada", "last_name": "Lovelace", "unsubscribed": false, "created_at": "2026-11-14T08:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

```json domain.updated
{
  "type": "domain.updated",
  "created_at": "2026-11-14T08:05:00.000Z",
  "data": { "id": "d91e...", "name": "mail.acme.com", "status": "verified", "region": "eu-west-1" }
}
```

All email events share `email_id`, `from`, `to`, `subject` and `created_at`, plus `tags` (as an object) when the email had tags and `broadcast_id` for broadcast emails. `email.bounced` adds `bounce`, `email.clicked` adds `click`, `email.failed` adds `failed: { reason }`. The `email.received` payload is shown in [Receiving email](/docs/receiving).

## Verify signatures

Every request is signed with the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) scheme, using three headers:

| Header | Contains |
| --- | --- |
| `webhook-id` | A unique event id, like `evt_8c1...`. The same for retries of one event |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Unix time in seconds when this attempt was sent |
| `webhook-signature` | `v1,<base64 signature>` (several, space-separated, during secret rotation) |

The signature is HMAC-SHA256 of `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${raw body}`, keyed with the base64-decoded part of your secret after `whsec_`. Always verify against the **raw** body, before any JSON parsing, and reject timestamps more than five minutes old.

```ts Node.js
import { verifyWebhook } from "delivrie";

// Next.js route handler, Hono, Workers... (Express: use express.raw and pass req.body)
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  try {
    const event = await verifyWebhook({
      payload: await req.text(),
      headers: req.headers,
      secret: process.env.DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
    });
    await handle(event);
    return new Response("ok");
  } catch {
    return new Response("invalid signature", { status: 400 });
  }
}
```

```python Python
from delivrie import verify_webhook, WebhookVerificationError

# Flask; in Django pass request.body, in FastAPI await request.body()
try:
    event = verify_webhook(request.get_data(), request.headers, os.environ["DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"])
except WebhookVerificationError:
    return "", 400
```

```go Go
body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
event, err := delivrie.VerifyWebhook(body, r.Header, os.Getenv("DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"))
if err != nil {
	http.Error(w, "invalid signature", http.StatusBadRequest)
	return
}
```

```php PHP
try {
    $event = \Delivrie\Webhook::verify(file_get_contents('php://input'), getallheaders(), getenv('DELIVRIE_WEBHOOK_SECRET'));
} catch (\Delivrie\Exception\WebhookVerificationException $e) {
    http_response_code(400);
    exit;
}
```

Each SDK checks the signature and the timestamp and returns the parsed event.

No SDK in your language? The [Ruby](/docs/ruby) and [Rust](/docs/rust) guides show the check written by hand, and Standard Webhooks libraries (`standardwebhooks` on npm and PyPI, and others) also work with your `whsec_` secret.

## Respond quickly

Return any `2xx` status within 15 seconds. Do slow work (database writes, calling other APIs) in a background job after responding. Redirects aren't followed and count as failures.

## Retries

Failed deliveries (non-`2xx`, timeout, connection error) are retried with increasing gaps: after about 5 seconds, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 5 hours, then every 10 hours, for up to 72 hours.

- Events can arrive more than once and out of order. Use `webhook-id` to skip duplicates, and `created_at` to order them.
- See every attempt, with the status code and response, on the endpoint's page in [Webhooks](https://delivrie.io/webhooks) or with `GET /webhooks/:id/events`.
- Resend any attempt with **Replay** or `POST /webhook-deliveries/:id/replay`.
- Check your endpoint with **Send test event** or `POST /webhooks/:id/test`.

## Test locally

Expose your local server with a tunnel such as `ngrok http 3000` or `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000`, add the tunnel URL as an endpoint, then send to a [test address](/docs/test-mode) to trigger real events.


---

# Broadcasts

Send newsletters and announcements to a segment of contacts with Delivrie broadcasts: personalisation, topics, unsubscribe links, test sends and scheduling, from the dashboard or the API.

A broadcast sends one email to every subscribed contact in a [segment](/docs/contacts): newsletters, product announcements, policy updates. Each recipient gets their own copy with their name filled in and their own unsubscribe link.

## From the dashboard

1. Open [Broadcasts](https://delivrie.io/broadcasts) and click **New broadcast**.
2. Choose a verified sender, a segment and, optionally, a [topic](/docs/contacts) so people can opt out of just this kind of email.
3. Write it in the editor. Use `{{first_name}}` or any contact property.
4. **Send test** to up to five inboxes and check it on your phone.
5. **Send now** or **Schedule**.

## With the API

```bash
# 1. Create a draft
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/broadcasts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "November newsletter",
    "from": "Acme <news@mail.acme.com>",
    "subject": "What we shipped in November",
    "segment_id": "SEGMENT_ID",
    "preview_text": "Three new features and a discount",
    "html": "<p>Hi {{first_name|there}},</p><p>...</p><p><a href=\"{{{unsubscribe_url}}}\">Unsubscribe</a></p>"
  }'

# 2. Send it now, or schedule it with an ISO 8601 time
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/broadcasts/BROADCAST_ID/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "scheduled_at": "2026-11-20T08:00:00Z" }'
```

The send response includes `recipients`, the number of contacts it will go to. Cancel a scheduled broadcast with `POST /broadcasts/:id/cancel` (it goes back to draft).

| Request | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `PATCH /broadcasts/:id` | Edit a draft: `name`, `from`, `reply_to`, `subject`, `preview_text`, `segment_id`, `topic_id`, or `html` to replace the content |
| `POST /broadcasts/:id/duplicate` | Copy any broadcast as a new draft, optionally with a new `name` |
| `GET /broadcasts/:id/recipients` | Before sending: who it will reach. After: who it went to, with `delivered`, `opened`, `clicked`, `bounced` and `unsubscribed` for each person. Filter with `status`, page with `limit` and `offset` |
| `GET /broadcasts/:id/links` | Every clicked link with total and unique clicks, most clicked first (click tracking must be on for the domain) |
| `DELETE /broadcasts/:id` | Delete a broadcast that isn't sending |

Broadcasts send [webhook events](/docs/webhooks) as they move along: `broadcast.created`, `broadcast.updated`, `broadcast.scheduled`, `broadcast.canceled`, `broadcast.sending`, `broadcast.sent` (with its stats) and `broadcast.deleted`.

## Who receives it

Every contact in the segment, except contacts who:

- are unsubscribed,
- are on your [suppression list](/docs/suppressions), or
- opted out of the broadcast's topic.

## Personalisation

| Variable | Inserts |
| --- | --- |
| `{{first_name}}`, `{{last_name}}`, `{{email}}` | The contact's details (escaped). `first_name` falls back to "there" when empty |
| `{{plan}}`, `{{city}}`, ... | Any [contact property](/docs/contacts), with the fallback you set for that property |
| `{{first_name\|friend}}` | A fallback just for this email |
| `{{{unsubscribe_url}}}` | The recipient's unsubscribe page |

## Unsubscribing

Every broadcast email gets `List-Unsubscribe` and one-click unsubscribe headers, so Gmail and Apple Mail show their own **Unsubscribe** button. Include a visible link too, with `{{{unsubscribe_url}}}`. The page it opens lets people unsubscribe from everything or from one topic, and you can brand it in Settings.

## Broadcasts vs. API sends

Use broadcasts for the same message to many people. For one-to-one messages triggered by something a user did (receipts, password resets, alerts), use [`POST /emails`](/docs/send-email) or an [automation](/docs/automations).


---

# Contacts, segments and topics

Store your audience in Delivrie: create and import contacts, custom properties, segments for broadcasts and automations, and topics for granular unsubscribes.

Contacts are the people you send broadcasts and automations to. They belong to your team, and each email address appears once.

## Create or update a contact

`POST /contacts` creates a contact, or updates it if the email already exists, so it's safe to call on every sign-up. For an existing contact, only the fields you send change: names and `unsubscribed` are replaced, `properties` are merged, and anything you leave out is kept. Someone who unsubscribed stays unsubscribed unless you send `"unsubscribed": false`:

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/contacts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "ada@example.com",
    "first_name": "Ada",
    "last_name": "Lovelace",
    "properties": { "plan": "pro", "city": "London" },
    "segments": ["SEGMENT_ID"]
  }'
```

```ts Node.js
await delivrie.contacts.create({ email: "ada@example.com", first_name: "Ada", properties: { plan: "pro" } });
```

Get, update or delete a contact by id **or** email address:

```bash
curl https://delivrie.io/api/contacts/ada@example.com -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"

curl -X PATCH https://delivrie.io/api/contacts/ada@example.com \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "properties": { "plan": "scale" }, "unsubscribed": false }'
```

`properties` in an update are merged into the existing ones; other properties are kept.

## Import

Upload a CSV in [Contacts → Import](https://delivrie.io/contacts/import). Map columns to email, first name, last name and properties, and choose a segment to add everyone to. Only import people who agreed to hear from you.

With the API, `POST /contacts/imports` takes CSV text (with an `email` column) or a list of contacts, up to 50,000 at a time. It runs in the background:

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/contacts/imports \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "csv": "email,first_name,plan\nada@example.com,Ada,pro\nsam@example.com,Sam,free", "segment_ids": ["SEGMENT_ID"] }'
```

Columns other than `email`, `first_name`, `last_name` and `unsubscribed` become properties (`plan` above). Rename or skip columns with `columns`, like `{ "E-mail": "email", "Company": "property:company", "Notes": null }`. Set `update_existing: false` to leave contacts that already exist as they are. Check progress with `GET /contacts/imports/:id` (it reports `created`, `updated`, `skipped` and the first 100 errors), list recent imports with `GET /contacts/imports`, or listen for the `contact.import.completed` [webhook](/docs/webhooks).

## Properties

Properties hold anything you want to personalise or filter by: plan, city, signup date. Define them, with a type and fallback value, in [Contacts → Properties](https://delivrie.io/contacts/properties). `GET /contact-properties` lists them. Use them in broadcasts as `{{plan}}`.

## Segments

Segments are named groups of contacts. Broadcasts go to a segment, and automations can start when someone joins one.

| Request | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /segments` with `{ "name": "Beta users" }` | Create a segment |
| `GET /segments` | List segments |
| `GET /segments/:id` | One segment with its contact count |
| `PATCH /segments/:id` with `{ "name": "Customers" }` | Rename a segment |
| `GET /segments/:id/contacts` | List the contacts in a segment (`limit`, `offset`) |
| `POST /segments/:id/contacts` with `{ "contacts": ["ada@example.com", { "email": "sam@example.com", "first_name": "Sam" }] }` | Add contacts, creating any that don't exist |
| `DELETE /segments/:id/contacts` with `{ "contacts": ["ada@example.com"] }` | Take contacts out of the segment (emails or ids). `DELETE /segments/:id/contacts/:email` removes one |
| `DELETE /segments/:id` | Delete the segment (the contacts stay) |

## Topics

Topics let people opt out of one kind of email (say, product updates) without leaving everything. Create them in [Contacts → Topics](https://delivrie.io/contacts/topics) with a default of opt-in or opt-out, then pick a topic when you create a broadcast. The unsubscribe page shows each topic as its own switch. `GET /topics` lists them.

## Unsubscribed contacts

A contact with `unsubscribed: true` gets no broadcasts. It happens when they click unsubscribe, when they mark a broadcast as spam, or when you set it. Transactional emails sent with `POST /emails` aren't affected; they're for messages the person needs, like receipts.


---

# Automations and events

Send emails automatically when something happens: record events with POST /events, build automations with waits, conditions and branches, and create simple flows with the API.

Automations send emails on their own when something happens: a welcome series after sign-up, a nudge three days after a trial starts, a receipt when an order is paid. Your app sends an **event**; any live automation listening for it starts a **run** for that contact.

## 1. Send events from your app

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "event": "user.signed_up", "email": "ada@example.com", "data": { "plan": "free", "first_name": "Ada" } }'
```

```ts Node.js
await delivrie.events.send({ event: "user.signed_up", email: "ada@example.com", data: { plan: "free", first_name: "Ada" } });
```

```python Python
requests.post("https://delivrie.io/api/events", headers=auth, json={
    "event": "user.signed_up", "email": "ada@example.com", "data": {"plan": "free"},
})
```

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | Lowercase letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores, like `order.paid` |
| `email` | The contact it's about. The contact is created if it doesn't exist |
| `data` | Optional JSON, up to 32 KB. Use it in conditions and templates |

The response says how many automations started: `{ "object": "event", "id": "...", "event": "user.signed_up", "runs": 1 }`. Sending access keys can send events. See recent events in [Events](https://delivrie.io/events), or with `GET /events` (event names) and `GET /events?name=user.signed_up` (recent events with that name).

## 2. Build an automation

In [Automations](https://delivrie.io/automations), create one and pick a trigger:

- **An event**, like `user.signed_up`
- **A contact joining a segment**

Then add steps:

| Step | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Send email | Sends a published [template](/docs/templates) |
| Wait | Pauses for minutes, hours, days or weeks |
| Condition | Branches on event data or contact properties |

Choose whether a contact can go through it once or every time the trigger happens, then **Publish**. Use **Test** to run it for one address without affecting stats.

## Create one with the API

The API creates straight-line automations (send and wait steps). Build branches in the dashboard.

```bash
curl -X POST https://delivrie.io/api/automations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Welcome series",
    "trigger": { "event": "user.signed_up" },
    "steps": [
      { "type": "send", "template_id": "welcome" },
      { "type": "wait", "amount": 2, "unit": "days" },
      { "type": "send", "template_id": "getting-started-tips" }
    ],
    "reentry": "once",
    "publish": true
  }'
```

`template_id` takes a template id or alias, and a send step can override `from` and `subject`. Up to 30 steps. Use `{ "segment_id": "..." }` as the trigger to start when someone joins a segment.

Manage automations with `GET /automations`, `GET /automations/:id` (with run counts), `GET /automations/:id/runs`, and `POST /automations/:id/publish`, `/pause` and `/resume`. `POST /automations/:id/duplicate` copies one, with its trigger and steps, as a new draft. `PATCH /automations/:id` renames it (`name`, `reentry`) and `DELETE /automations/:id` deletes it.

## Runs

Each contact going through an automation is a run: `running`, `completed`, `failed` or `canceled`. Open an automation to see every run and each step's timing. If a step fails (for example, the template's sender domain isn't verified), fix the cause, then retry or skip the step from the run.

## Event data in templates

Templates sent by an automation can use the contact's details and the triggering event's data. For the event above, `{{first_name}}` and `{{plan}}` both work, and so does the longer form `{{data.plan}}`, including nested fields like `{{data.order.total}}`. Add a fallback with `{{plan|free}}`. In automations, every variable is HTML-escaped.


---

# Audit logs

See who changed what in your Delivrie team and when: sign-ins, members, API keys, domains, webhooks, single sign-on, connected apps, billing and content. Enterprise plan.

The audit log records who changed what in your team, and when. It's part of the **Enterprise** plan. Delivrie records activity for every team, so the full history is there as soon as you upgrade.

Team admins open it from **Settings → Audit log**. Entries can't be edited or deleted, by you or by us through the dashboard, and you can export them as CSV for security reviews.

## What's recorded

| Area | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Sign-ins | Every sign-in to the dashboard, with the method (password, code, Google, GitHub, SSO) |
| Members and access | Members added or removed, role changes, invites sent or revoked, single sign-on changes, apps connected or disconnected |
| API keys | Keys created, renamed or deleted (never the key itself) |
| Domains | Domains added or removed, settings changed, DNS checks, Cloudflare setup |
| Webhooks | Endpoints added, changed or deleted, test events |
| Billing | Plan changes, cancellations, spending cap, auto top-up and billing details |
| Content and sending | Templates published or deleted, broadcasts sent or scheduled, automations published or paused, suppressions removed, contacts deleted |

Each entry shows **who** did it (a person, an API key, a connected app, or the system for changes confirmed by the payment provider), **what** changed, the **target** (for example the domain name), and the IP address when the change came through the API.

Sending email isn't a change to your account, so individual sends aren't in the audit log; they're in [Logs](https://delivrie.io/logs) and on each email's page. Only the names of the fields that changed are recorded, never secrets or message content.

## With the API

`GET /audit-logs` returns the newest entries first.

```bash
curl "https://delivrie.io/api/audit-logs?limit=50&action=api_key." \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DELIVRIE_API_KEY"
```

| Query | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `limit` | 1 to 200, default 50 |
| `before` | An entry `id`: returns older entries (for paging) |
| `action` | Only actions starting with this, e.g. `domain.` or `billing.plan_changed` |
| `actor` | Only entries by this user id or API key id |

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "has_more": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "audit_log",
      "id": "1842",
      "created_at": "2026-11-23T14:02:11.000Z",
      "actor_type": "user",
      "actor_label": "ada@acme.com",
      "action": "api_key.created",
      "target_type": "api_key",
      "target_label": "Production",
      "metadata": { "permission": "sending", "prefix": "dlv_7Hk2" },
      "ip": "102.89.34.10",
      "user_agent": "Dashboard"
    }
  ]
}
```

Teams on other plans get `403 plan_required`. The endpoint needs a full-access API key.


---

# Troubleshooting and FAQ

Answers to the most common Delivrie questions: emails not arriving, going to spam, API errors, webhooks not firing, SMTP connection problems, limits and billing.

## Sending

**My request returns 200 but the email never arrives.**
Open the email in [Emails](https://delivrie.io/emails) (or `GET /emails/:id`) and check its status:
- `suppressed`: every recipient is on your [suppression list](/docs/suppressions).
- `bounced`: the event says why; usually the address doesn't exist.
- `failed`: the `error` field says why, often that the sending domain stopped being verified.
- `delivered`: the recipient's server accepted it. Ask them to check spam and any filters; see the [Deliverability guide](/docs/deliverability).
- `queued` or `sent` for more than a few minutes: check [status](https://delivrie.io/status), then contact us.

**I get "The from domain ... is not verified".**
The domain in `from` must be verified in this team. Check for typos (`mail.acme.com` vs `acme.com`), check the key belongs to the right team, and see [Why isn't my domain verifying?](/docs/domain-not-verifying) While testing, use `onboarding@delivrie.io`.

**I get "... can only send to members of your team".**
You're sending from `onboarding@delivrie.io`, which can only email your teammates and the [test addresses](/docs/test-mode). Verify your own domain to email anyone.

**Can I send from Gmail, Yahoo or Outlook addresses?**
No. You can only send from domains you own and verify. Those providers' DMARC policies would send such mail to spam anyway.

**Emails go to spam.**
Follow [If mail goes to spam](/docs/deliverability). Most often it's a new domain with no history, missing DMARC, or content that looks promotional.

**How do I send to many people at once?**
For different content per person, use [batch sending](/docs/send-email) (100 per request). For the same message to a list, use [broadcasts](/docs/broadcasts). Don't put many recipients in one email's `to`: they'd all see each other.

**Is there a request rate limit?**
There's no fixed per-second limit today. Plan limits are on emails per day and month: see [Plans and limits](/docs/limits). For large sends, use batches or broadcasts rather than thousands of parallel requests.

## API and code

**401 errors.**
`missing_api_key`: the `Authorization` header is missing, often because the environment variable isn't set where the code runs. `invalid_api_key`: the key was deleted, mistyped, or has extra spaces or quotes around it.

**403 restricted_api_key.**
A sending access key can only send. Use a full access key for other endpoints, or check the key's domain restriction.

**CORS errors in the browser.**
Don't call the API from the browser; your key would be public. See [CORS and browser apps](/docs/cors).

**"Request body must be valid JSON".**
Send `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body. In cURL, check your quotes; in code, use `JSON.stringify` or your client's JSON option.

**Where can I see exactly what I sent?**
[Logs](https://delivrie.io/logs) has every API request with its request and response bodies, including failures.

## Webhooks

**My endpoint isn't receiving events.**
Check the endpoint is subscribed to those events and enabled, uses `https://`, is publicly reachable (not `localhost`), and returns `2xx` within 15 seconds without redirecting. The endpoint's page in [Webhooks](https://delivrie.io/webhooks) shows each attempt with its status code and response. Use **Send test event** to try it.

**Signature verification fails.**
You're almost certainly verifying a parsed and re-serialised body. Verify the raw body, exactly as received, and use the right endpoint's `whsec_` secret. See [Verify signatures](/docs/webhooks).

**I get the same event twice.**
Retries can deliver an event more than once. Skip events whose `webhook-id` you've already handled.

## SMTP

**Connection times out.** Your host probably blocks port 587 or 465. Use `2587` or `2465`. See [SMTP](/docs/smtp).

**535 authentication failed.** The username must be `delivrie` and the password a valid API key.

## Account and billing

**What happens when I reach my limit?** See [When you reach a limit](/docs/limits).

**Can I change plans any time?** Yes, in [Billing](https://delivrie.io/billing). Everyone pays in US dollars by card through Stripe.

**How long are emails and logs kept?** Email content, sent and received, and API request logs: 30 days on every plan. Recipients, status and events stay after content is deleted. Use [webhooks](/docs/webhooks) to keep your own records.

**Can several people use one account?** Yes: invite teammates in Settings. Free includes one member; Starter and Pro five; Scale unlimited.

## Still stuck?

- Ask in the chat in the bottom corner of the dashboard. Replies arrive there and by email.
- Email [support@delivrie.io](mailto:support@delivrie.io) with the email id or request id from [Logs](https://delivrie.io/logs), so we can find it quickly.
- Check [status](https://delivrie.io/status) for anything affecting everyone.


---

# API reference

Base URL `https://delivrie.io/api`. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer dlv_your_key`.


---

# Send email

`POST https://delivrie.io/api/emails`

Send a transactional email. Returns the email id immediately; delivery events arrive through webhooks and the Logs page.

Access: Sending or full access. MCP tool: `send_email`.

## Headers

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | string | Yes | Bearer token. Any API key works, including sending-only keys. |
| `Idempotency-Key` | string | No | Unique key for this request. Retrying with the same key returns the original email instead of sending again. |

## Body

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | Yes | Sender address on a verified domain. Use "Name <email@domain>" to set a display name. |
| `to` | string \| string[] | Yes | Recipient address or up to 50 addresses. |
| `subject` | string | Yes | Email subject line. Optional when you send a template. |
| `html` | string | No | HTML body. Provide html, text or template. |
| `text` | string | No | Plain-text body. Generated from html when omitted. Default: `auto`. |
| `cc` | string \| string[] | No | Carbon-copy recipients. |
| `bcc` | string \| string[] | No | Blind carbon-copy recipients. |
| `reply_to` | string \| string[] | No | Where replies go. |
| `template` | object | No | Send a published template: { "id": "alias-or-id", "variables": { … } }. |
| `scheduled_at` | string | No | ISO 8601 date or a phrase like "in 1 hour" or "tomorrow at 9am" (UTC). Up to 30 days ahead. |
| `tags` | object[] | No | Name/value pairs attached to the email and its webhook events. Letters, numbers, _ and - only. |
| `headers` | object | No | Custom email headers. |
| `attachments` | object[] | No | { filename, content } with base64 content. Up to 40 MB per email. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "from": "Acme <orders@acme.com>",
    "to": [
      "ada@example.com"
    ],
    "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
    "html": "<p>Thanks for your order!</p>",
    "tags": [
      {
        "name": "category",
        "value": "receipt"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "id": "4ef9a417-02e9-4d39-ad75-9611e0fcc33c"
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Name | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No Authorization header was sent. |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | The key doesn't exist or was deleted. |
| 403 | `restricted_api_key` | This sending key is limited to a different domain. |
| 422 | `validation_error` | A required field is missing or malformed, or the from domain isn't verified on this team. The message says which. |
| 429 | `daily_quota_exceeded` | Free plan limit of 133 emails a day reached. |
| 429 | `monthly_quota_exceeded` | Free plan monthly limit reached and no credits left. |
| 429 | `spending_cap_reached` | This send would take overage past your spending cap. |


---

# Send batch

`POST https://delivrie.io/api/emails/batch`

Send up to 100 emails in one request, each with its own recipients and content. Batch emails can't have attachments or scheduled_at.

Access: Sending or full access. MCP tool: `send_batch`.

## Headers

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | string | Yes | Bearer token. |
| `Idempotency-Key` | string | No | Makes the whole batch safe to retry. |

## Body

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[ ]` | object[] | Yes | An array of up to 100 email objects with the same fields as Send email. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails/batch' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '[
    {
      "from": "Acme <orders@acme.com>",
      "to": [
        "ada@example.com"
      ],
      "subject": "Receipt",
      "html": "<p>Order 1</p>"
    },
    {
      "from": "Acme <orders@acme.com>",
      "to": [
        "sam@example.com"
      ],
      "subject": "Receipt",
      "html": "<p>Order 2</p>"
    }
  ]'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "4ef9a417-…"
    },
    {
      "id": "9a1c22b0-…"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Name | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 422 | `validation_error` | More than 100 emails, or an email uses attachments or scheduled_at. |


---

# Retrieve email

`GET https://delivrie.io/api/emails/:id`

Get one email with its status and every delivery event.

Access: Needs a full access key.. MCP tool: `get_email`.

## Headers

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | string | Yes | Bearer dlv_your_key |

## Path parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Yes | The email id. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X GET 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails/4ef9a417' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "object": "email",
  "id": "4ef9a417-…",
  "from": "Acme <orders@acme.com>",
  "to": [
    "ada@example.com"
  ],
  "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
  "last_event": "delivered",
  "created_at": "2026-11-12T09:12:04Z",
  "events": [
    {
      "type": "sent"
    },
    {
      "type": "delivered"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Name | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No Authorization header was sent. |
| 404 | `not_found` | Nothing with that id on this team. |


---

# Update email

`PATCH https://delivrie.io/api/emails/:id`

Reschedule an email that hasn't been sent yet.

Access: Sending or full access.

## Headers

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | string | Yes | Bearer dlv_your_key |

## Path parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Yes | The email id. |

## Body

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scheduled_at` | string | Yes | New send time: ISO 8601 or a phrase like "in 2 hours". |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X PATCH 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails/4ef9a417' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "scheduled_at": "tomorrow at 9am"
  }'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "object": "email",
  "id": "4ef9a417-…"
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Name | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 422 | `validation_error` | Only scheduled emails can be updated. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails/4ef9a417/cancel' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "object": "email",
  "id": "4ef9a417-…"
}
```

## Errors

| --- | --- | --- |

# List emails

`GET https://delivrie.io/api/emails`

List sent emails, newest first.

Access: Needs a full access key.. MCP tool: `list_emails`.

## Headers

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | string | Yes | Bearer dlv_your_key |

## Query parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | number | No | Results per page, 1 to 100. Default: `50`. |
| `offset` | number | No | How many results to skip. Default: `0`. |
| `direction` | string | No | outbound or inbound. Default: `outbound`. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X GET 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "4ef9a417-…",
      "subject": "Your order is confirmed",
      "last_event": "delivered"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Name | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No Authorization header was sent. |
| 404 | `not_found` | Nothing with that id on this team. |


---

# List received emails

`GET https://delivrie.io/api/emails/received`

Emails that arrived on your receiving domains, newest first. Fetch one with Retrieve email for its HTML and text.

Access: Needs a full access key.. MCP tool: `list_received_emails`.

## Headers

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | string | Yes | Bearer dlv_your_key |

## Query parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | number | No | Results, 1 to 100. Default: `50`. |
| `to` | string | No | Only mail sent to this address. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X GET 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails/received' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "a5c3e1f0-…",
      "from": "Ada <ada@example.com>",
      "to": [
        "support@in.acme.com"
      ],
      "subject": "Re: Your order",
      "created_at": "2026-11-14T10:22:30Z",
      "attachments": [
        {
          "filename": "photo.jpg",
          "content_type": "image/jpeg",
          "size": 248213
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Name | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No Authorization header was sent. |
| 404 | `not_found` | Nothing with that id on this team. |


---

# List attachments

`GET https://delivrie.io/api/emails/:id/attachments`

The files of a sent email with download links. For received mail use GET /emails/received/:id/attachments. Links last an hour; files are kept for 30 days, like email content. GET /emails/:id/attachments/:attachment_id returns one.

Access: Needs a full access key.. MCP tool: `list_attachments`.

## Headers

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | string | Yes | Bearer dlv_your_key |

## Path parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Yes | The email id. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -X GET 'https://delivrie.io/api/emails/4ef9a417/attachments' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dlv_live_••••'
```

## Response

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "attachment",
      "id": "att_1",
      "filename": "invoice.pdf",
      "content_type": "application/pdf",
      "size": 48213,
      "download_url": "https://…/attachments/…?token=…",
      "expires_at": "2026-11-28T10:12:04Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Errors

| Status | Name | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No Authorization header was sent. |
| 404 | `not_found` | Nothing with that id on this team. |


---
